SHIPPED AND HARDWARE-VERIFIED. 24 kHz superwideband runs end to end today; treat it as a constraint you build on, not an open question.

Downlink: the model's own 24 kHz PCM goes straight to Opus with NO resampling anywhere. 12 kHz of delivered bandwidth. 9 kHz sibilance arrives at -22.6 dB where it was previously folded onto 7 kHz.

Framing, not sample rate, was the thing that failed before. The earlier 24 kHz attempt used 20 ms frames = 50 packets/s against a chip that can start about 48.8 decodes/s. At 60 ms frames it is 16.7/s and fits. A second cause was that libopus had been compiling -Os the whole time: target_compile_options put -O3 before Zephyr's flags so the command line read "-O3 -Os" and the last -O won. Applied as a source property it wins; text 255K -> 316K, encode 20.4 -> 16.4 ms.

Costs are MEASURED on-device with a 32.768 kHz counter around each call, not estimated: decode 8.8 ms/packet at 16 kHz, 25.2 ms at 24 kHz, encode 15.0 ms/call. That is about 87% of one 64 MHz core, which is why the uplink encoder runs at complexity 0 — uplink audio only has to be understood by speech-to-text, while the decoded downlink is what the owner actually hears. mic_drops went 29 -> 7 of 931.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all of them numbers you can re-measure rather than judgements:
- Alias rejection on any resampling stage >= 60 dB. The 16 kHz path's 2-tap average gave 3.2 dB; the polyphase windowed-sinc FIR that replaced it gives 67.5 dB. Measure with scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs.
- Codec cost under 100% of one 64 MHz core, with the measurement taken on-device.
- mic_drops under about 1% of blocks.
- tx_starved at or near zero. Last hardware run: "agent 24 kHz down", 284 packets decoded, tx_starved 3.
- No audible content before the agent speaks. The sync preamble used to be played as audio — 4 bursts of 16 samples at 0x6C6C (~85% of full scale) 20 ms apart, i.e. loud clicks at the start of every conversation. Post-fix the same press-moment capture is peak 0, 0 nonzero samples of 22050.

Do not propose work premised on 24 kHz being unavailable, on the SoC being too slow for it, or on needing a resampler in the downlink path. If you want to change the audio path, the bar is a measurement from scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs or an on-device counter, not an argument.

America/New_York. That is this Mac's system zone, read from /etc/localtime, currently EDT (UTC-4).

Scope this correctly, because it is the part that has been getting confused: it is authoritative for anything RESOLVED ON THIS MAC — routine firing times, quiet hours, "this morning", file timestamps, calendar reads. It is not a claim about where the owner is standing. The pendant has never been given a zone: NITZ was never captured, no GNSS receiver is started (CONFIG_LOCATION and CONFIG_GNSS are unset and nrf_modem_gnss appears zero times in the firmware), and the device clock arrives as zoneless digits. Code that parses those digits must return a null instant rather than borrowing this zone — catchupSources.js and voiceNotes.js both already refuse it, and that refusal is correct.

If you need the owner's own timezone as distinct from the machine's, that is still an open question for the owner and you should say so rather than substituting this value for it.

Answer from reading the source. THERE IS NO QUEUED-ACTION RESUME POLICY, AND THERE IS ALSO NO RESUME. The decision engine you would need is already written and is excellent; nothing calls it. Your stated fallback is the right default — but two of the premises behind it are wrong in ways that will change your design, so read sections 3 and 4 before encoding a resume gate.

=== 1. REVERSIBLE vs IRREVERSIBLE: classified in code, in three separate vocabularies. Use riskTier and replaySafety, not "reversible".

(a) foreseeAction — local-agent/planPreview.js:106 -> {reversible: true|false|null,
    reversedBy, irreversibleReason, typeReversibility}. Backed by a static table in
    local-agent/actionReceipts.js:75-87 producing 'conditional' | 'always' | 'never' |
    'not-needed'. HARD_TO_REVERSE = new Set(['delete_path']) — planPreview.js:41.

(b) riskTierFor — local-agent/actionLedgerVerify.js:219-231. THIS is the tier the ledger and
    the approval both key on. Exact strings:
        'uncontained' · 'off-machine' · 'observe' · 'setting' ·
        'irreversible-write' · 'reversible-write'
    Hardcoded membership at actionLedgerVerify.js:181-208. Note :230 — when foreseeAction
    returns reversible:null it falls through to 'irreversible-write', deliberately
    pessimistic, with the header (:15-22) citing the real incident where undo deleted a
    user's file.

(c) replaySafetyFor — actionLedgerVerify.js:168-174 -> 'idempotent' | 'additive' |
    'unrepeatable' | 'unknown'. Hardcoded sets at :69-121 (idempotent), :126-136 (additive),
    :140-166 (unrepeatable).
    *** THIS IS THE AXIS RESUME ACTUALLY TURNS ON, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME AS REVERSIBILITY. ***
    Your request frames the gate as reversible-vs-irreversible. The code that would
    implement resume asks a different and better question: can this be REPLAYED without
    doing it twice. A reversible action can still be unrepeatable (sending the same message
    twice is undoable and still wrong), and an irreversible one can be idempotent. Encode
    the gate on replaySafety, and use riskTier for the approval question.

(d) classifyAction — local-agent/actionRisk.js:150-167 -> {safe, reason}. Hardcoded
    AUTO_SAFE_ACTIONS Set (:11-89), CONFIRM_REASONS Map (:91-105), STATUS_SHELL_PATTERNS
    (:111-129), SHELL_METACHAR (:108).

=== 2. THE DURABLE RECORD EXISTS AND IS WELL BUILT

local-agent/actionLedger.js. On disk: ledgerLocation() (:98-103) = env
PENDANT_ACTION_LEDGER_PATH or path.join(workspacePath, '.pendant-action-ledger.json');
workspacePath = PENDANT_WORKSPACE_PATH || ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace (config.js:30-32).
Durability is real — writeJsonAtomic (atomicJsonStore.js) fsyncs the file AND the directory.
The stated ordering invariant (actionLedger.js:43-52) is that the inflight record is fsynced
BEFORE the executor is handed the action, so "pending" provably means "never dispatched."
That invariant is the foundation any resume policy should rest on.

Manifest fields (:354-370): version, ledgerId ('ldg_<uuid>'), planKey, jobId, sessionId,
source, command, title, status, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt, outcome, risk, steps.
Step fields (buildStep, :264-303): seq, stepKey, actionId, type, label, effect, touches,
reversible, reversedBy, irreversibleReason, riskTier, replaySafety, needsApproval,
approvalReason, sensitivity, withheldParams, sensitiveParams, intent, params, preState,
resumable, notResumableReason, phase, startedAt, finishedAt, ok, status, message, receiptId,
postState.
Two independent state axes:
    manifest status  'open' -> 'settled'          (:363 open; closeLedger default :455)
    step phase       'pending' -> 'inflight' -> 'done'   (:295, :413, :436)
NEITHER IS AN ENUM. closeLedger takes an arbitrary string ({status='settled'} at :455, no
validation), and step .status is String(result?.status ?? (result?.ok===false ? 'failed' :
'success')) at :439 — whatever the handler returned. There is no 'failed' PHASE; failure is
phase:'done' + ok:false.
Bounds are LOSSY and the module says so: MAX_STORE_BYTES 1 MiB, MAX_LEDGER_BYTES 64 KiB
(:81-82). Over budget, SHED_ORDER ['params','postState','preState','touches'] (:93) drops
fields and MARKS THE STEP resumable:false, counted as droppedLedgers/droppedThrough. So byte
pressure silently converts resumable work into non-resumable work — a resume policy has to
treat that as a real, expected state, not an error.

=== 3. RESUME AFTER OUTAGE: THE ENGINE EXISTS, THE TRIGGER DOES NOT

Implemented and good:
    planResume            actionLedgerVerify.js:727-844
    resumeLedger          actionLedger.js:585-589
    interruptedLedgers    actionLedger.js:496-508
    decision vocabulary   'completed' | 'skip' | 'rerun' | 'ask' | 'blocked'
                          (RESUME_DECISIONS, actionLedgerRoutes.js:32; produced by decideStep,
                           actionLedgerVerify.js:626-708)
    safety rule           once any step decides 'ask', EVERY LATER STEP IS 'blocked'
                          (planResume:752-759)

Complete list of production callers, from grep:
    interruptedLedgers -> actionLedgerRoutes.js:91   GET /ledger/interrupted
    resumeLedger       -> actionLedgerRoutes.js:118  GET /ledger/:ledgerId/resume
That is all. Both are GET, both return executed:false, and both files carry comments
explicitly forbidding execution (actionLedgerRoutes.js:24-29 and :103-116).

The startup block, local-agent/server.js:2226-2270, runs purgeAllCaptures(),
startRoutineScheduler(), resumeFocusSessions(), startPageWatchScheduler(),
startInputReachabilityMonitor(), launchBridge(). NO LEDGER SCAN. NO PENDING-ACTION SCAN. NO
REPLAY.
So resume today requires a human to already know a ledgerId, GET /ledger/:id/resume, and
hand-POST the returned runnable array to /execute.

*** AND THE DISCOVERY QUERY IS SATURATED WITH FALSE POSITIVES. ***
orchestrator.js imports only {ledgerStepObserver, openLedger} (orchestrator.js:11) and calls
openLedger at :532. THERE IS NO closeLedger CALL IN IT. Repo-wide the only production
closeLedger caller is visionLoop.js:296. Since interruptedLedgers() defines interrupted as
status==='open' || steps.some(phase==='inflight'), and every ordinary orchestrator run leaves
status:'open' forever, GET /ledger/interrupted RETURNS EVERY PLAN EVER RUN, and
planResume().interrupted (actionLedgerVerify.js:828-829) is true for completed runs.
formPreview.js:365 and prepareApprove.js:113 also open-and-never-close.
Any auto-resume built today would attempt to resume every plan that has ever succeeded.
Fixing orchestrator to call closeLedger is a PREREQUISITE, not a nice-to-have.

Also relevant to "after a browser or Mac outage": THERE IS NO JOB LEASE ON THE RELAY.
claimNextJob (cloud-relay/store/d1Store.js:753, memoryStore.js:224) does a compare-and-set
UPDATE ... SET status='processing' WHERE job_id=?1 AND status='queued', stamping
claimedBy/claimedAt. No lease_until column, no expiry, no requeue sweep;
cloudflare-worker/schema.sql:31 (relay_jobs) has no lease columns. A Mac that dies mid-job
leaves the row at 'processing' until JOB_TTL_MS (cloud-relay/config.js:18 = 24 h) prunes it.
Leases exist for exactly ONE thing — routines: lease_owner/lease_until on relay_routines,
claimDueRoutines({leaseMs = 300_000}) at d1Store.js:887 / memoryStore.js:297. That is the
working template if you propose an intent lease.
The browser side DOES have a real lease: COMMAND_LEASE_MS = 45_000
(local-agent/browserBridge.js:11) with orphan detection at :575-597; also COMMAND_TTL_MS
90_000 (:26), IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS 10 min (:37), MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_KEYS 500 (:38),
ONLINE_WINDOW_MS 70_000 (:10). But note startBrowserBridgeSupervisor is imported at
local-agent/server.js:26 AND NEVER CALLED — the 30s sweep that expires those leases does not
run; the only path to sweepBrowserBridge() is a manual POST /browser/sweep.

=== 4. THE APPROVAL SIDE: three mechanisms, and the one you would key a "fresh spoken approval" on CANNOT COMPLETE

(a) THE LIVE PATH IS A DEAD END. bridge.js:345 runs classifyPlan(plan.actions). If autoRun,
    it POSTs /execute. Otherwise bridge.js:422-424 sets
        plan.executed = false
        plan.awaitingApproval = verdict.blocked
        plan.response = ... || 'Waiting for your approval on the dashboard.'
    THERE IS NO DASHBOARD APPROVAL. grep -rn "awaitingApproval" src/ dist/ returns ZERO
    hits; the React dashboard has no Approve control; nothing ever reads awaitingApproval
    back to execute it. The only consumers are pendantSpeech.js:89-95 (phrasing) and
    cloud-relay/jobRecall.js:134-138 (a status label). A blocked plan is SPOKEN ABOUT AND
    THEN DISCARDED — the actions exist only inside the job-result object. This is the
    clearest silent no-op in the tree: the sentence promises an affordance that does not
    exist. If your capability speaks "I'll wait for your approval," it will inherit that lie
    unless you build the other half.

(b) prepare/approve is COMPLETE, HTTP-WIRED, AND STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE.
    local-agent/prepareApprove.js + shared/approvalHandoff.js, mounted at
    local-agent/server.js:33 + :1370 -> POST /prepare, GET /prepare/:ledgerId/world,
    POST /approve.
    IT HAS A REAL LEASE, which is exactly what your intent-lease capability wants:
        APPROVAL_DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000   shared/approvalHandoff.js:67
        APPROVAL_MIN_TTL_MS     = 60_000           :68
        APPROVAL_MAX_TTL_MS     = 2 h              :69   clamped by clampTtl (:481-485)
        expiresAt stamped :571; enforced :733-739 -> refuse('expired', ...)
    AND IT IS BOUND TO THE ACTION, NOT A LOOSE FLAG — five independent bindings, all in
    evaluateApprovalGrant (:712-810):
        planDigest   sha256 over per-step {seq,type,riskTier,reversible,touches,intent}
                     computed :189-208, enforced :779-784, refusal 'plan-changed'
        world        sha256 over per-step pathMark (path/existed/directory/bytes/sha256/
                     hashSkipped; MTIME DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED) :236-268, enforced :786-793,
                     refusal 'world-moved'
        confirmWord  planDigest last nibble -> 1 of 16 words, :212-215, vocab :107-124,
                     matched by matchApprovalUtterance :637, refusal 'unclear'
        replay guard state !== 'pending' -> 'already-decided' (:726-731)
        deliveredAt  the readback must have been spoken; markApprovalDelivered :843,
                     enforced :752-757, refusal 'not-delivered'
    Plus planKeyFor(supplied) !== manifest.planKey -> 'plan-changed' (prepareApprove.js:269).
    Confirm word is mandatory when any step's tier is in WORD_REQUIRED_TIERS =
    ['irreversible-write','off-machine','uncontained'] (:80-84), OR type is delete_path
    (ALWAYS_CONFIRMED_TYPES, :514), OR pendingCount > 1 (:497). The file is honest that this
    is a disambiguator, not an authenticator (:99-106).
    Record states: 'pending' (:573) -> 'granted' (:819) | 'denied' | 'refused' (:834).

    *** THE RELAY HALF IS SCHEMA-ONLY, SO THE LOOP CANNOT CLOSE. ***
    APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT (shared/approvalHandoff.js:965-971) is a FROZEN OBJECT OF STRING
    DESCRIPTIONS, e.g. 'saveState(approvalStateKey(id), record)'. It is documentation, not
    code. Nothing implements it — grep -rn "approval" cloud-relay/ returns only jobRecall.js
    reading the unrelated awaitingApproval field. These exports have NO production importer
    anywhere: approvalStateKey, approvalIndexKey, indexApproval, selectApprovalToSpeak,
    markApprovalDelivered, approvalControlFrame, approvalSpeech, MAX_INDEXED_APPROVALS.
    (prepareApprove.js:141-143 calls approvalStateKey/approvalIndexKey only to ECHO KEY NAMES
    back in the HTTP response — it stores nothing.)
    Because nothing persists the record and nothing speaks the readback, deliveredAt is NEVER
    SET in production, so evaluateApprovalGrant REFUSES EVERY GRANT at :753 with
    'not-delivered'. The prepare/approve loop is uncompletable by any code path in this repo
    today.
    The file itself documents why: PENDANT_DELIVERY_REALITY (prepareApprove.js:66-79) records
    that the firmware drops binary downlink unless convo_started is set and strstr-matches
    only "started", "flush", "end" — there is NO UNPROMPTED PUSH — and it lists the four
    firmware changes needed. THIS IS THE HARD BLOCKER ON "a fresh spoken approval". You
    cannot ask the owner out of the blue; the device cannot receive the ask.
    Also: prepareAction() has NO CALLER other than its own route handler
    (prepareApprove.js:482). Neither bridge.js nor orchestrator.js ever prepares anything.
    And there is NO PRIVILEGE SEPARATION: httpPolicy.js:13-22 makes only /health,
    /dashboard*, /assets/*, favicons public; everything else sits behind the single
    AGENT_TOKEN. /approve is gated by EXACTLY THE SAME CREDENTIAL as /execute — anything that
    can approve could already just execute. On the Mac the approval adds auditability, not
    authority.

(c) formPreview IS THE ONE APPROVAL THAT ACTUALLY WORKS. local-agent/formPreview.js, routes
    approveFormPreview (:1251) and markFormPreviewSubmitted (:1284).
        PREVIEW_TTL_MS = 20 * 60_000 (:86), hardcoded, not overridable
        confirm code is scrypt-hashed: CONFIRM_KDF {N:8192, r:8, p:1, maxmem:32MiB} (:420-425)
        states 'awaiting-approval' (:549,:807) -> 'approved' (:938) -> 'submitted' |
               'submit-failed' (:1025); revocable (:1116)
        expiry enforced :911; double-approve rejected :903
    If you want a working precedent for an expiring, action-bound approval, this is it.

=== 5. A COMPLETE CRASH-RECOVERY ENGINE WITH NO PRODUCTION CALLER

local-agent/workbenchTransaction.js (768 lines) implements exactly what your capability
needs: staged writes, same-filesystem atomic rename, directory fsync, a durable commit
record, rollback from snapshots, and IDEMPOTENT RE-RUN — planTransaction returns
decision:'retry' for any context not 'committed' (:127), so an interrupted job re-runs in
full and a completed one is skipped. Backed by local-agent/executionContext.js with statuses
'open' (:190), 'staging', 'committed' (:226), 'failed', 'adopted' (:336,:357), store at env
PENDANT_WORKBENCH_PATH (executionContext.js:68-71), MAX_CONTEXTS 240 / MAX_STORE_BYTES
256 KiB (:53-54).
commitTransaction IS NEVER CALLED outside workbenchTransaction.test.js. sweepStagingDirectories
likewise. server.js:1409 mounts only registerWorkbenchRoutes(app), and the comment directly
above at server.js:1406 admits it: "Plan and hand off durable jobs. Nothing here commits —
commitTransaction...". workbenchRoutes.js imports only planTransaction and verifyOutputs.
Meanwhile briefing.js and meetingPrep.js still call writeFileSync straight onto final paths —
the precise failure this module was written to prevent (its header, :24-27).
Note also: executionContext.js is NOT VALID UTF-8 — it contains a NUL byte and `file` reports
it as data.

Related: local-agent/handleThisRoutes.js:19-22 says outright "server.js is owned by someone
else right now, so nothing here is mounted yet." Confirmed — registerHandleThisRoutes has no
importer. handleThis.js, handleThisRoutes.js, handleThisPanel.js and handleThisReconcile.js
(~1,900 lines) are entirely dead in production.

=== 6. WHAT IS NOT A RESUME MECHANISM, so you do not mistake it for one

  contextResume.js — rehydrates CONVERSATION CONTEXT across model bodies. Every failure
    returns {resumed:false} and starts cold (:89-91); header: "Nothing in this file may fail
    a job." RESUME_TIMEOUT_MS 2500, env CONTEXT_RESUME_TIMEOUT_MS (:19).
  retryPolicy.js — 59 lines, pure in-memory. createRetryBackoff (base 250 ms, max 30 s,
    jitter 0.2) and createRateLimitedErrorReporter (30 s window). Used ONLY at bridge.js:127
    and :131 for the relay work-loop reconnect. Nothing to do with replaying actions.
  browserSpool.js — explicitly NOT a retry queue; header :20-25 "Nothing here is ever handed
    back to an extension automatically." It records what was DROPPED. Store
    .pendant-browser-spool.json (:28), MAX_SPOOL_BYTES 256 KiB (:40). Replay is a thing the
    owner asks for by hand.
  briefingQueue.js — a REVIEW queue for briefing findings; statuses 'waiting' | 'reviewed' |
    'dismissed' (:206-218). Its own comment (:203-205): "There is deliberately no 'acted' —
    nothing in this feature acts."
  meetingPrepQueue.js — an AUDIO PLAYBACK queue (QUEUE_BUDGET maxItems/maxSeconds, :57).
  goalRouter.js — pure routing decision, zero persistence. policyRouter.js — a model COST
    tier picker (TIER_DETERMINISTIC/TIER_BACKGROUND/TIER_PLANNER, :41-43); its header states
    it is "a COST decision, never a capability decision. Nothing here can refuse a request."
    NO approval or queueing policy lives there.

=== 7. UNDO, since a resume gate usually leans on it

local-agent/undo.js, wired at server.js:154, routes server.js:705 (undo last) and :770 (undo
by job id). Covers (undoOneResult :110-233): write_file/create_note/delete_path via SNAPSHOT
RESTORE (restoreFromSnapshot :237-256); write_file/create_note fallback delete ONLY IF THE
JOB CREATED THE FILE (guarded by item.receipt.preexisting?.existed at :168-170, the fix for
the incident in actionReceipts.js:17); set_brightness/set_volume/set_mute restore recorded
before; show_screen_overlay SIGTERM the pid; copy_path and move_path with clobber restore;
open_app/open_url/open_path/open_folder BEST-EFFORT CMD-W KEYSTROKE (:214-228) — a guess, not
an undo, it closes whatever window is frontmost.
DOES NOT COVER: run_shell, run_applescript, computer_use_task, send_email, send_message,
type_text, press_keys, all browser_*. Reported via irreversibleSteps (:90-98).
Limits: SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES 8 MiB (actionReceipts.js:34) — larger files are not snapshotted
and the action is recorded irreversible; one-shot via job.undoneAt (:29-31); WHOLE-JOB ONLY,
completed jobs only (:64-66); KEYED TO THE JOB STORE, NOT THE LEDGER — no undo of a manifest,
no undo of a resumed run, and no ledgerId -> undo link. The two records meet only through
step.receiptId (actionLedger.js:445).

=== 8. WHERE NO POLICY EXISTS AT ALL — state these as open decisions, do not invent them

  - No automatic resume policy. Nothing decides when, whether, or how often to continue an
    interrupted run. The engine can answer the question; nothing asks it.
  - No expiry on ledger records — only a byte budget. An approval can outlive its manifest;
    prepareApprove.js:360-367 handles that with 'plan-missing' rather than guessing, which is
    correct but means a valid approval can become uncommittable through pruning alone.
  - No authorization boundary between approving and executing (one AGENT_TOKEN).
  - No enum enforcement on closeLedger status or step .status.
  - No rate limit or lockout on wrong confirm-word attempts.
  - No policy on stale 'inflight' steps — nothing ever times one out or reconciles it; a step
    can sit inflight forever.

=== 9. WHAT I WOULD ENCODE

Your fallback — require fresh approval for all irreversible actions, auto-resume only
reversible ones with an unexpired lease — is the right DEFAULT and I am not overriding it.
Keep it, and surface it as an owner decision rather than a constant. Three corrections
before you encode it:
1. Key the auto-resume gate on replaySafety ('idempotent'|'additive' may auto-resume;
   'unrepeatable'|'unknown' may not), and key the approval requirement on riskTier
   (WORD_REQUIRED_TIERS is already the right set). "Reversible" alone is the wrong axis and
   the codebase already knows it.
2. "A fresh spoken approval" is NOT AVAILABLE. The pendant cannot receive an unprompted push
   — PENDANT_DELIVERY_REALITY, prepareApprove.js:66-79 — and deliveredAt is never set, so
   every grant refuses with 'not-delivered'. Design the gate so that a pending approval waits
   for the owner's NEXT conversation rather than assuming it can interrupt.
3. Two prerequisites, both small and both blocking: orchestrator.js must call closeLedger
   (otherwise every completed plan looks interrupted), and relay_jobs needs a lease_until
   plus a requeue sweep (the routine lease at d1Store.js:887 is the template). Say these are
   prerequisites rather than proposing a lease that sits on top of a saturated signal.
Finally, do not propose the storage: shared/approvalHandoff.js already has the TTL, the plan
digest, the world fingerprint, the confirm word and the refusal vocabulary. What is missing
is a relay implementation of APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT and a delivery path — name those as the
dependency.

context.topic: owner's intended timezone for personal routines and 'morning/evening' language
context.text:
OWNER DECISION. America/New_York is this Mac's zone and is authoritative for anything resolved on the Mac. The owner travels, so the two records that disagreed (memory said America/Chicago) were both describing something real and neither was the answer.

The rule: routines fire on the MAC's zone, and any owner-facing time is labelled when the owner is somewhere else. "Every morning at 7" means 7am where the Mac is. Do not silently reinterpret a routine because the owner moved — a promise that shifts under them is worse than one that is occasionally in the wrong zone, because they cannot predict it.

The pendant still has no zone of its own and must not be given one by inference: no NITZ is captured, no GNSS receiver is started, and its clock arrives as zoneless digits. Code that parses those must return a null instant rather than borrowing the Mac's zone. catchupSources.js and voiceNotes.js already refuse this and are correct.

This is a default, not a discovered fact. Design so the zone is a value that can be changed, not a constant compiled in.

OWNER DECISION, and it is narrower than the question assumed.

Tasks and reminders are NOT this system's data. POST /reminders writes into macOS Reminders; the owner deletes them in Apple's app and nothing here is involved. Voice notes already have DELETE /voice-notes/:noteId, which removes the words and reaps the audio. Both are solved and neither needs a policy.

The real subject is the thing the owner never created: facts this system EXTRACTS on its own from what was said, into facts.json and the context graph. The owner cannot see that list, so they cannot ask for a specific item to be removed, and that — not deletion mechanics — is the actual defect.

So the policy is: anything extracted without being asked for must be listable and individually deletable, or it must not be extracted. Prefer showing over remembering. If a fact cannot be surfaced to the owner in a form they would recognise, that is a reason not to store it rather than a storage problem to solve.

Scope of an erase, when one is asked for: the extracted fact AND its derived copies AND the evidence capsule it came from. NOT the job history — that is the owner's audit trail, the record of what this system did on their Mac, and deletion and accountability want opposite things here. Deleting the evidence of an action is a different act from forgetting a fact, and must be asked for separately.

Audio follows the existing rule and no new one: it goes to microSD only when an upload could not be delivered, and the SD copy is removed on acknowledgement.

Off-machine (relay D1 rows, R2 audio) is in scope for an erase but is replicated and cannot be promised as instantaneous. Report it as requested-and-pending rather than as done.

context.topic: current USB serial audio/session integration status
context.text:
You are asking the right question and the answer resolves the fork you set up - but not to either branch. It is not "a working serial bridge exists, propose wiring", and it is not "the parser is the immediate implementation blocker". It is: USB conversation continuity is not missing work, because it is not work.

The owner's standing answer: USB is for flashing firmware and bench testing only. It is not a product transport and never will be. So do not treat a Mac-side serial audio session as a gap to close, do not schedule the parser as a blocker, and - as you already suspected - do not claim the owner can talk locally today. The correct claim is stronger than "not today": not over USB, ever. Note this governs regardless of the earlier acceptance of usb_fallback_audio_session (s13-u35s); that skill's premise is the one being corrected here, so do not spend further rounds implementing it.

WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS on the Mac side, measured on this checkout tonight, so you never have to ask again:

Log capture and flashing, in shell, and nothing else.
- diagnostics/start_dual_capture.sh - "Simple dual UART capture for nRF9160 + ESP32", both at 115200 baud, writing to a timestamped directory. Log capture, not a session.
- diagnostics/dual_chip_autocapture.sh - the same idea with port autodiscovery over /dev/cu.usbmodem* and /dev/cu.usbserial*.
- firmware/nrf9160/scripts/auto_capture_diag.sh - UART diagnostic capture for the nRF9160.
- firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge/flash.sh - flashing, defaulting to PORT=/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA.

There IS a line-oriented JSON control channel, but it lives entirely on the ESP32 side: firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge/src/main.cpp reads characters at :1129 and parses each line with deserializeJson at :942. That is a control protocol for bench commands. It is not an audio path and there is no counterpart on the Mac.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST, checked rather than assumed:
- No serial library anywhere in the project. "serialport" appears in no package.json in this repository.
- No host-side serial reader/writer module in software/ at all - no Node, no Python, nothing the agent can call.
- No framing parser for audio over serial, and no session coordinator.
- Nothing serial in the capability manifest. I checked the live inventory: 219 routes and 99 action types, and the words serial, usb, tty and baud appear in NONE of them.
- The only programmatic path to a port is action:run_shell - "Run any shell command on the Mac (zsh)" - through POST /execute. And that route "returns no ledger id, so its receipts and the ledger cannot be joined afterwards", and "a receipt carries no exit code, no command line and no environment". So even a shell-based serial step cannot tell you why it failed.

So the honest status line is: a bench log capture exists at 115200 on both chips, a flashing path exists, an ESP32-side JSON control protocol exists, and there is no Mac-side serial reader, no framing parser, no session coordinator, and no capability that reaches a port. Three of the other agents asked for that reader tonight; one bounded read-only version was granted to mac-terminal (t22-ib1b) for BENCH use, and the other three were denied, including one that wanted an open read/write session between the hardware and the relay.

Where to put the round instead. The continuity problem you are circling is real; USB is just the wrong answer to it. The durable primitives already exist and are not transport-specific: POST /workbench/contexts claims a piece of work "so a restart can tell a retry from a second attempt" and returns the same context for the same job and intent rather than duplicating it; GET /workbench/jobs/:jobId/handoff reports "what a run that was interrupted and restarted had already finished, packaged so another machine can pick it up"; GET /workbench/contexts/:contextId reports what actually landed on disk versus what a step claims. Those solve continuity across an interruption without a cable, which is the version of the problem the product will actually have.

tools.name: mac_workspace_edit
tools.why: Useful work will require implementing and testing the owner's requested 24 kHz superwideband pendant audio path and other code changes in ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace. Existing Mac actions can run limited shell commands but do not expose a safe, structured multi-file edit/test workflow with diffs and receipts.

root.description: Workspace root, constrained to an approved project directory such as /Users/evanliu/AI-Pendant-Workspace or /Users/evanliu/agentic-gadget/software/ai-pendant-simulator

tools.name: audio_pipeline_validate
tools.why: The owner’s stated goal is to ship the 24 kHz superwideband path end to end. Reconnaissance confirms 24 kHz WAV output, but we lack a safe, read-only validator that checks capture→relay→TTS→pendant/bridge formats, resampling, frame timing, clipping, and round-trip continuity against the acceptance criteria.

pipeline_id.description: Existing pipeline run ID to validate; if omitted, choose the newest completed audio run.

checks.description: Checks to perform; defaults to all safe checks.

tools.name: audio_link_fault_inject
tools.why: The live measurements show simultaneous uplink/downlink loss, and the requested 24 kHz path cannot be responsibly shipped without repeatable fault-injection across modem, relay, and codec. Existing discovery exposes no tool that can run this end-to-end test.

tools.name: fleet_health_and_repair
tools.why: The current system exposes raw /ops/status but no typed, callable health diagnosis or safe repair operation. This capability is needed to turn offline-browser and missing-permission failures into fast, resumable owner-facing recovery instead of repeated timeouts.

tools.name: commitment_evidence_query
tools.why: The proposed promise tracker cannot safely decide whether an uttered commitment was completed using generic browser/Mac actions alone. It needs one least-privilege, provenance-preserving query that searches only explicitly bound tabs/apps and returns evidence candidates without mutating anything.

target.description: Specific tab/session URL pattern or app/path binding

tools.name: privacy_convergence_check
tools.why: The proposed privacy latch needs a read-only, cross-surface verification after a local button press; existing Mac/browser action tools do not provide a single authenticated receipt proving that capture, playback, relay persistence, queued jobs, and browser exposure are all stopped.

tools.name: incident_diagnostics
tools.why: The proposed cross-surface diagnosis capability cannot be implemented with the current seven tools: it needs a read-only, correlated snapshot of pendant/relay/Mac/browser evidence and a dry-run repair plan without granting mutation access.

deviceSkills.name: local_privacy_latch
deviceSkills.what_it_does: On a long press of sw0, immediately mute playback, stop microphone capture, set a persistent privacy-latched flag, and drive a distinctive LED pattern. A second long press clears it only after a local confirmation pattern; the flag survives link loss and reboot until explicitly cleared. Emit only a tiny enter/exit state event when LTE-M is available.

deviceSkills.name: physical_transaction_approval_latch
deviceSkills.what_it_does: When a staged transaction is pushed to the pendant, the device enters a clearly marked pending state. A deliberate 1.5-second hold of the single button followed by release emits exactly one approval event containing the staged transaction nonce; a short press cancels. The LED uses a distinct slow-double-flash pending pattern and a rapid flash for approved/cancelled. It never submits anything itself; it only emits an offline-safe, replay-resistant approval/cancel event when linked, or retains the decision until reconnect.

deviceSkills.name: usb_fallback_audio_session
deviceSkills.what_it_does: When USB serial is present and LTE is unavailable, expose the existing microphone/button/audio framing to the Mac as a local conversation transport. Maintain monotonic frame and turn sequence numbers, pause LTE retries while USB owns the session, and hand ownership back only at a turn boundary so audio is not duplicated.

proposals.user_asks: Let me interrupt you naturally while you’re speaking—when I start talking, stop the reply, listen to what I said, and continue from there without making me press the button again.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is currently effectively half-duplex: the owner must wait through speech or use the single button. Barge-in makes it usable in real life, especially when a reply is long, wrong, or unsafe to act on. It relies on the pendant for immediate acoustic interruption, the relay for stream cancellation, and the Mac/voice model for a fresh turn; no single node can provide a responsive, coherent experience alone.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-realtime-2.1 for the active turn and interruption transcript; no additional model call for VAD/cancellation. Use a cheaper background model only to summarize abandoned speech turns for diagnostics, if enabled.
proposals.latency_budget: Local playback duck/stop within 120 ms of voice onset; relay cancellation within 300 ms; new listening state announced or captured within 500 ms. Engineering time is dominated by race-proofing cancellation, packet sequencing, and testing LTE-M loss—not inference.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible incremental API cost for the interrupted turn (the already-running realtime stream is cancelled); modest extra audio uplink for the new turn. Main cost is implementation and test coverage, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Raw microphone audio remains on the pendant/relay path under existing retention policy; accidental household speech could trigger interruption. Keep VAD local, upload only after speech onset, discard the cancelled assistant audio, and require confirmation only if the interrupted reply had an irreversible action pending.
missing: Local playback-side VAD with an interrupt event and debounce
A relay protocol carrying generation IDs plus idempotent cancel/ack
Mac bridge support for cancelling queued TTS and publishing an interruption receipt
A user-visible setting for sensitivity and a test fixture for speech-over-TTS in LTE-M loss conditions

proposals.user_asks: Give me a spoken emergency stop for the whole hive: when I say my private stop phrase, immediately cancel queued Mac/browser work, revoke pending approvals, stop outgoing audio, and tell me exactly what was prevented or already irreversible.
proposals.why_useful: Today cancellation is surface- or job-specific and may require reaching the Mac. A worn-device stop phrase gives the owner a reliable last-resort control when a browser action looks wrong, the pendant is misplaced, or a queued routine starts behaving unexpectedly. It is useful precisely because the relay stays awake, the pendant is always with the owner, and the Mac/browser may be remote or asleep.
proposals.model_tier: No realtime model call for recognition after a local wake/phrase detector; use a small fixed command grammar and relay-side authentication. Use the expensive realtime tier only if the phrase is unclear, never to decide whether an emergency stop is valid.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant should enter a local muted/stop state within 150 ms; relay revocation fan-out within 500 ms when online; Mac/browser acknowledgements within 2 seconds. Cost is dominated by reliable fan-out and recovery testing, not inference.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per invocation: one authenticated control message and a few metadata receipts. No audio upload is needed for a confident local phrase match.
proposals.security_concerns: A thief or nearby speaker must not be able to trigger or learn the phrase. Store only a salted verifier/derived local matcher, support an optional button-held gesture for high assurance, rate-limit attempts, and never speak sensitive job details until the owner re-authenticates. Stopping cannot undo an already submitted external action; the response must distinguish cancelled, blocked, and irreversible.
missing: A pendant-local fixed-phrase detector and authenticated emergency control frame
Relay-wide revocation registry with monotonic epoch numbers
Mac/browser hooks that subscribe to revocation epochs and terminate queued/active work
A dashboard recovery flow to review what was stopped and re-enable normal operation

proposals.user_asks: When something goes wrong, let me press and hold the pendant to capture an incident packet; when my Mac is reachable, turn it into a sourced bug report draft with the audio, UART/pipeline evidence, timestamps, and a one-sentence spoken receipt—never submit it without approval.
proposals.why_useful: The owner already wants the pendant to file its own bug reports, but a wearable can capture the moment while the Mac is unavailable. This joins offline SD buffering, LTE-M relay delivery, Mac workspace evidence, and a reviewable draft instead of losing the failure or forcing the owner to reconstruct it later.
proposals.model_tier: Use firmware for button timing, ring-buffer capture, checksums, and offline queue; relay/background worker for authenticated upload and deduplication; mac-terminal for bounded read-only UART/log and pipeline collection; mac-planner for low-cost incident summarization and draft generation; realtime only for the immediate spoken acknowledgment.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local haptic/voice acknowledgment under 300 ms; upload opportunistically after link recovery; Mac draft within 60 s of the Mac becoming reachable. The owner reviews and explicitly approves any issue submission.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per incident depending on audio duration and summarization; storage and bandwidth dominate, not the short acknowledgment. Keep a configurable 30–90 s compressed audio window and delete after the draft is accepted or expires.
proposals.security_concerns: Incident audio and local logs may contain private speech, tokens, or personal data. Encrypt the SD packet and relay object, redact secrets from logs, bind packets to the paired device, show exactly which files/snippets leave the pendant, and require confirmation before creating an external ticket or sending anything. Recovery is an idempotent packet ID and a local retained copy until the owner chooses deletion.
missing: A firmware long-press/incident capture event and bounded pre-roll audio ring buffer
A relay endpoint for resumable encrypted incident packets with idempotency and retention controls
A narrowly scoped read-only Mac workspace/UART/log collector (not arbitrary shell)
A draft review surface that displays evidence provenance and an approve/send checkpoint
A readiness gate and delivery receipt so the pendant does not claim the report exists while the Mac agent is not ready

proposals.user_asks: When I say “save my place,” capture what I’m doing across the pendant, Mac, and logged-in browser; later, when I say “resume,” restore the relevant tabs and workspace, summarize what changed while I was away, and put me at the next safe step without submitting or sending anything.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can lose the thread between a wearable interruption, a Mac workspace, and private browser tabs. This would create a durable, privacy-aware handoff that survives a dropped connection and returns them to work rather than merely reporting device status or replaying a generic briefing.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize the checkpoint and compute changes; use the realtime model only for the spoken command and concise receipt. Mac and browser agents perform deterministic capture/restoration, while the relay stores the encrypted checkpoint and queues it offline.
proposals.latency_budget: A checkpoint receipt under 2 seconds when connected, with an offline pendant acknowledgment under 300 ms. Resume should restore and present a reviewable plan within 10 seconds; never wait on a long model call before acknowledging capture.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.04 per resume, dominated by summarizing changed page/workspace state. Checkpoints themselves are small structured metadata and should not duplicate full page contents or audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, tab titles, drafts, and focused-app state are sensitive. Encrypt checkpoints, bind them to the paired device, store only hashes and minimal snippets by default, expire them automatically, and require confirmation before any restoration that could overwrite unsaved work. Browser actions must be provenance-labeled and reversible; no email, form, purchase, or deletion may be performed as part of resume.
missing: A cross-surface checkpoint schema with stable tab/session identifiers, Mac workspace references, pendant event IDs, timestamps, and sensitivity labels
A relay-backed encrypted checkpoint store with offline queueing, TTL, conflict versions, and deduplicated diffs
Browser session reattachment and a restore transaction that previews tabs/actions before applying them
A Mac workspace snapshot/restore adapter that can detect unsaved changes and refuse destructive replacement
A change summarizer that compares checkpoint state with current state using hashes and small evidence snippets
A pendant command/status protocol for save, queued, synced, conflict, and resumed states

proposals.user_asks: “Keep the conversation understandable when the connection gets bad, and make sure I don't lose what I said or what you said.”
proposals.why_useful: The current LTE-M half-duplex path demonstrably drops about 7.8 seconds of uplink during simultaneous speech. This gives the owner graceful degradation instead of silent loss: the pendant reports quality locally, the relay negotiates a smaller/ordered audio mode, the Mac can recover the missing intent from a transcript, and the owner gets a short spoken completion/recovery receipt rather than guessing whether the system heard them.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-4.1-mini for packet-loss classification, transcript reconciliation, and receipt generation; gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the live turn and interruption decisions; gpt-5.6-luna on the Mac only if recovery requires a multi-step browser or filesystem action.
proposals.latency_budget: Local packet-loss/jitter detection under 100 ms; relay mode switch within one 60 ms audio frame; no more than 250 ms added to live speech. Recovery receipt within 5 s after link restoration. Background transcript reconciliation can take seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.02 per affected call, dominated by any recovery transcription/reasoning; healthy calls add negligible model cost because quality decisions are deterministic telemetry.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio and packet diagnostics leave the pendant over TLS as they do today; SD is used only as the existing failed-upload buffer and must be encrypted or cryptographically erased after delivery. Never replay recovered private text aloud without the owner's normal conversation authorization; browser actions remain gated by existing destructive-action confirmation. Persist only sequence numbers, loss windows, hashes, and a short-lived transcript pointer by default.
missing: A versioned audio-session protocol with sequence numbers, timestamps, acknowledgements, jitter-buffer targets, and negotiated bitrate/sample-rate modes
Pendant firmware telemetry and a local LED/error pattern for degraded mode, plus bounded SD spool metadata and replay deduplication
Relay-side selective retransmission/FEC policy that respects the ~2 kB TLS record limit and half-duplex LTE-M behavior
A Mac bridge recovery endpoint that can reconcile partial voice turns and produce a completion receipt
End-to-end 24 kHz acceptance tests measuring intelligibility, loss concealment, latency, and CPU/RAM/power on the actual nRF9160 + ESP32 path

proposals.user_asks: “When I say ‘this’ while I’m looking at something on my Mac, use the pendant to bind my words to the exact browser tab or screen I mean, then tell me what it is and prepare the next step without making me describe or read it aloud.”
proposals.why_useful: Today voice, the Mac screen, and authenticated browser sessions are separate contexts, so deictic requests like “handle this” are ambiguous or fail. This would let the owner keep their eyes and hands on the work: a button press or short spoken marker creates a cryptographically linked handoff from the pendant’s utterance to the active Mac window/tab, while the browser supplies private-page evidence and the relay preserves the task if the Mac briefly disconnects.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the short live utterance and marker timing; gpt-4.1-mini for window/tab identity matching, OCR/DOM evidence alignment, and ambiguity scoring; gpt-5.6-luna on Mac for planning a multi-step follow-up. No expensive model is needed for the normal exact-match path.
proposals.latency_budget: Marker acknowledgement under 150 ms; active-tab identity and a first evidence snippet within 1 s; ask a spoken clarification within 2 s if confidence is below threshold. Preparing a multi-step action may continue asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per handoff, dominated by OCR or model-based ambiguity resolution; exact active-tab binding is deterministic and nearly free. Browser extraction and any later action are separate costs.
proposals.security_concerns: The binding must be scoped to the owner’s authenticated Mac session and expire quickly. Send tab ID, origin, title, and a minimal selected/visible-region hash to the relay—not arbitrary page contents—until the owner asks to inspect it. Never infer consent to submit, send, delete, purchase, or disclose secrets from the marker; preserve the existing confirmation gate. Dashboard and spoken receipts must redact sensitive values.
missing: A Mac accessibility/screen-observation adapter that emits the focused window, active tab, selection, and stable page-region identifiers with owner consent
A pendant-to-Mac marker protocol carrying monotonic time, utterance ID, and a one-button disambiguation event
A relay task-envelope format that joins audio, device event, Mac observation, and browser evidence with expiry and provenance
Browser-bridge support for returning a stable tab/session identity and a minimal DOM or screenshot-region proof
A user-facing ambiguity flow that offers ‘the tab I’m on’, ‘the selected text’, or ‘the window in front’ and lets one button choose among them

proposals.user_asks: “Keep my voice conversation intact even if LTE drops, and tell me plainly if anything had to wait.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can speak naturally while moving through coverage gaps instead of losing a turn or guessing whether the pendant heard them. It uses the pendant's SD only as a failure buffer, honoring the existing no-routine-storage rule, then drains and reconciles packets when the link returns.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna for relay reconciliation and concise receipts; gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the live conversational path; no model for packet buffering or acknowledgements.
proposals.latency_budget: Normal path adds under 100 ms for packet acknowledgement. During an outage, local capture is immediate; replay begins within 2 seconds of link recovery. The owner hears one short status sentence only when continuity was affected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost in the normal path; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per recovered turn for reconciliation depending on transcript size. Dominant cost is LTE data and relay/R2 writes, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Temporary Opus chunks and sequence metadata leave the pendant only after upload; failed chunks remain on removable SD until delivered or explicitly wiped. Encrypt the failure buffer with a device-held key, cap retention/size, and require no confirmation for automatic retry but confirmation before exposing recovered content in a new external action.
missing: Firmware packet journal with authenticated monotonically increasing sequence numbers and bounded SD quota
Relay resumable upload endpoint with acknowledgements, deduplication, and ordered replay
Bridge/relay session state that distinguishes delayed audio from a new turn
A small dashboard view and spoken status event for buffered/replayed packets
End-to-end test harness that injects LTE loss during capture and playback

proposals.user_asks: “If I missed what you said, repeat the last answer—or give me the short version—even when the connection has already dropped.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable conversation should remain recoverable in the moment. The owner can tap or say “repeat” while walking, in noise, or after a brief disconnection instead of losing the answer and restarting the whole request. This is distinct from buffering a new turn: it recovers the most recently delivered response locally and can provide a compact fallback when full replay is impractical.
proposals.model_tier: No model for exact local replay. Use gpt-5.6-luna only when a short cached text summary must be generated before delivery; use gpt-realtime-2.1 only if the owner asks a new conversational follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: Exact replay starts within 150 ms of the button gesture. A cached short version starts within 500 ms when available. No network round trip is required for the common case.
proposals.cost_estimate: Zero model cost for replay; occasional summarization is approximately $0.001–$0.01 per response and should happen once when the response is first generated, not on each replay. Storage and LTE costs are negligible because only one bounded response is retained.
proposals.security_concerns: Retain only the latest response, encrypted, with an owner-configurable expiration and explicit wipe gesture. Do not retain microphone input for this feature. Dashboard should show whether a replayable response exists without exposing its text until requested.
missing: Pendant-side last-response ring containing compressed audio plus a short encrypted text label or summary
Relay/mac-bridge delivery protocol that marks audio as fully delivered and supplies replay metadata before playback ends
Offline button/voice handling for repeat versus new conversation
A bounded cache policy covering interruption, reboot, and power loss
Acceptance tests for replay latency, privacy wipe, and partial-response behavior

proposals.user_asks: “Remember this even if there’s no signal: …” — capture my spoken note on the pendant, then when it reconnects transcribe it, file it into ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace with source/time/location confidence, and tell me on the pendant exactly where it landed.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can safely capture thoughts while walking through LTE dead zones without keeping the thought in working memory. This is more than a voice memo: the pendant buffers only failed uploads, the relay resumes delivery, and the Mac turns the recovered utterance into a searchable, cited workspace artifact with a delivery receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the live capture acknowledgement and a short playback receipt; use a cheaper background transcription/extraction model on reconnect, and mac-planner gpt-5.6-luna only for filing/classifying into the workspace. No browser or iOS required for the core path.
proposals.latency_budget: Local capture acknowledgement under 150 ms. Reconnect upload is opportunistic and resumable; transcription/file receipt within 2 minutes of network recovery. If classification is ambiguous, save to Inbox rather than block delivery.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per short note, dominated by transcription and extraction; LTE airtime and SD writes dominate device energy, not inference. Background batching can reduce cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio remains on the SD only while upload is unavailable, encrypted-at-rest with a device key if supported; relay stores an expiring ciphertext/object and deletes it after confirmed Mac receipt. Sensitive notes must not be spoken back in public. Filing and receipt need no confirmation, but any extracted action that sends mail, changes calendar, or deletes data must enter the existing confirmation gate.
missing: A pendant offline-note mode with a bounded SD spool, chunk hashes, sequence numbers, and a local spoken/LED acknowledgement distinct from ordinary call audio
A reconnect upload protocol with resumable chunks and an idempotency key, plus relay-to-Mac delivery receipts and retry/dead-letter status
A Mac workspace filing endpoint that writes a markdown note plus JSON provenance sidecar under ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/Inbox and returns the final path
A device key / key rotation policy for SD-stored audio and an owner-visible retention/delete control

proposals.user_asks: “What am I looking at?” — use the pendant as the trigger, inspect the Mac’s current window (and the authenticated browser tab if that is the source), then answer aloud with the relevant text, controls, or next safe step without making any changes.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must stop, describe the screen, and manually bridge the wearable conversation to the Mac. This would make the pendant a genuinely hands-free context switch: a spoken question becomes an evidence-backed answer about the exact private page or app in front of them, while preserving the existing confirmation boundary for actions.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to recognize the short trigger and speak the answer. Use mac-vision gpt-4.1-mini for screenshot/UI grounding, browser-extension for DOM text and tab identity, and mac-planner gpt-5.6-luna only when reconciliation or a multi-step explanation is needed. Prefer extracted DOM text over sending screenshots to the expensive tier.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge locally in under 150 ms; return a first answer in 3 seconds for a normal app or browser page, with a 6-second ceiling before saying it is still inspecting. Never wait indefinitely on a stale browser extension.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per request, dominated by vision tokens; DOM-first routing and a short-lived screenshot reduce cost. No background calls unless the owner explicitly asks for follow-up.
proposals.security_concerns: The request may expose private browser content, passwords, messages, or financial data to model processing. Require an enrolled pendant session, show the active app/tab title before capture when practical, redact password fields and tokens at the Mac harness, keep screenshots/text ephemeral, and log only provenance hashes. Reading is allowed under the owner’s standing rule; clicking, typing, sending, purchasing, or deleting still requires the existing confirmation gate.
missing: A signed pendant-to-Mac context-request channel carrying request ID, freshness deadline, and cancellation
A Mac active-window capture/redaction service that can provide accessibility metadata and a screenshot without stealing focus
A browser bridge operation returning tab URL/title, selected DOM regions, and redacted text for the active tab
A unified evidence envelope (source surface, timestamp, screenshot/text hashes, confidence) and a realtime response stream
A clear owner-facing privacy indicator and policy for when private screen content is allowed to leave the Mac

proposals.user_asks: “Keep the conversation clear, and tell me if the connection or audio quality is degrading.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner should not have to guess whether silence, clipping, or delayed replies is their microphone, LTE-M, the relay, or the speaker. The worn device can measure local capture/playback health, the relay can see transport and decode timing, and the Mac/dashboard can retain a short diagnostic timeline. Together they can automatically stay at 24 kHz when viable, fall back gracefully when necessary, and give one brief spoken explanation instead of silently failing.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-realtime-2.1 for the live quality decision and one-sentence explanation only; no model call for telemetry thresholds, codec negotiation, or recovery. A cheaper background model may summarize recurring failures later if the owner asks.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 100 ms for local telemetry and codec-mode changes; under 300 ms for relay-to-pendant mode negotiation. Spoken warning should be at most one short sentence and should not interrupt an active utterance unless quality is unusable.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental API cost during healthy sessions because thresholds and negotiation are deterministic. Occasional realtime explanation is a few cents or less per incident; storage is a small bounded event record, not audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Transport metrics, battery state, and short-lived quality events leave the pendant and may be stored on the relay/Mac. Do not store raw microphone audio for diagnostics by default. The dashboard must redact network identifiers, cap retention, and require confirmation before uploading a diagnostic bundle or sharing it externally.
missing: A versioned audio-session telemetry schema shared by firmware and relay (sample rate, frame sequence, packet loss, jitter, decode/encode duration, underruns, battery, and selected mode).

A real 24 kHz end-to-end acceptance test that exercises capture, relay transcode, decode, I2S playback, and induced LTE loss; the currently documented path is asymmetric (15,625 Hz capture and 24 kHz playback).
A deterministic capability handshake and hysteresis policy for 24 kHz, narrowband fallback, and recovery so mode changes do not oscillate.
A dashboard quality timeline and a relay endpoint for bounded, owner-approved diagnostic export.

proposals.user_asks: “When I say private, make sure nothing from this room is sent anywhere, and tell me when it is safe to resume.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner cannot establish a trustworthy, immediate privacy boundary across a worn microphone, an active relay stream, and work continuing on the Mac/browser. This would provide a physical, understandable privacy state: the pendant cuts or locally buffers capture even if LTE is still connected; the relay revokes the session and rejects late frames; the Mac/browser pauses queued transcription or actions; and resumption requires an explicit spoken or button action. The owner gets a clear local cue and a verifiable receipt rather than hoping mute propagated.
proposals.model_tier: No model for enforcement: firmware and relay use a signed session-state transition. gpt-realtime-2.1 may generate only the short spoken confirmation after the state is verified. Background models are not involved.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant capture cutoff under 50 ms from the trigger; relay acknowledgement under 500 ms when connected. If disconnected, local privacy state must take effect immediately and remain authoritative until explicit resume.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost in normal use; a tiny authenticated state event per transition and bounded audit record. Optional later summaries use a cheaper background model, only if requested.
proposals.security_concerns: This must fail closed: no cloud interpretation of the privacy trigger, no raw audio retention while private, and no automatic resume. Session keys and monotonic counters must prevent replay of stale resume/mute messages. The dashboard should show state and receipt without exposing room audio or precise location. Browser jobs that already caused irreversible external effects cannot be undone, so they must be blocked at the action checkpoint before private mode is acknowledged.
missing: A hardware-local privacy control independent of the network (a long press or dedicated mute switch; the current single button is overloaded with conversation start/end).
A signed, monotonic privacy-state protocol shared by firmware, relay, Mac bridge, and browser job queue, including behavior for in-flight frames and disconnected operation.
A relay-side hard gate that drops audio before transcription/storage and a Mac/browser pause barrier for queued jobs.
A dashboard and spoken receipt that distinguish local mute, relay-confirmed mute, and safe-to-resume; this must be tested with LTE loss, process crash, and reconnect races.

proposals.user_asks: “If my pendant link gets bad, keep the conversation going through my Mac or phone and tell me only if I need to change anything.”
proposals.why_useful: LTE-M is half-duplex and the current prototype spends most of a core decoding and encoding; a wearer should not lose an important answer because the pendant is in a dead spot or overheating. The system can preserve the live turn, then return to the pendant when its link is healthy.
surfaces: pendant detects packet loss, modem state, battery/thermal signals, and plays a short local status tone
relay owns the session epoch, buffers a bounded amount of audio, chooses the active transport, and emits a handoff receipt
Mac menubar app takes over realtime audio when reachable; iOS app is the secondary transport when the Mac is absent
browser is not used for raw audio, but can remain available for any authenticated action already in progress
dashboard shows transport, reason, and whether any words were lost
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the active spoken turn only; no model call is needed to decide a transport handoff. Use a cheap background model only to summarize a turn if the owner explicitly asks after a disrupted session.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect degradation within 300 ms, switch transports within 1–2 seconds, and replay at most the last 2 seconds of assistant audio. The owner should hear no more than a brief earcon and one short sentence if manual action is required.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental model cost; bandwidth and relay WebSocket duration dominate. A small amount of encrypted session metadata per handoff is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio and session continuity must remain end-to-end scoped to the owner’s authenticated devices; never fall back to an unpaired browser. Buffer only a few seconds in memory, erase it after acknowledgement, rotate handoff tokens, and require confirmation before any queued browser/Mac side effect resumes after transport change.
missing: A production pendant with a reliable second transport or a defined BLE/Wi-Fi path to the Mac/phone
Native Mac and iOS realtime audio clients with background/lock-screen behavior
Relay session migration protocol with sequence/timestamp continuity and bounded encrypted audio buffer
A user-visible pairing and emergency 'stay on pendant' control
The pending 24 kHz acceptance criteria and hardware constraints to set realistic thresholds

proposals.user_asks: “While I’m in a meeting or driving, keep the pendant quiet, but let genuinely urgent things through as a one-sentence interruption—and give me everything else as a private queue afterward.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has scheduled briefs and spoken responses, but no coordinated interruption policy. This would prevent the pendant from becoming socially disruptive while preserving timely awareness of a critical calendar change, account warning, or explicitly urgent message.
surfaces: Mac planner reads the owner’s current calendar event, focus state, and local activity signals; it never infers driving from raw audio alone
browser extension reads only the authenticated notification sources the owner has explicitly enrolled
relay maintains the durable urgency queue, quiet hours, deduplication, and delivery receipts when the Mac is asleep
pendant receives only the approved one-sentence interrupt, a tactile/earcon severity cue, and a button action to defer or open the queue
dashboard and iOS show the queued items with source, reason for urgency, timestamp, and the policy that admitted or suppressed them
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to classify and deduplicate incoming items; use the realtime model only for the brief spoken interruption or when the owner asks follow-up questions. Deterministic calendar and policy rules should decide whether a source is eligible before any model call.
proposals.latency_budget: Urgency classification under 30 seconds for notifications and under 5 seconds for calendar changes. A permitted interruption should reach the pendant within 3 seconds; suppressed material can wait for the owner’s next review.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: background classification is the dominant API cost, roughly a few cents per active day depending on notification volume. The relay queue and receipts add negligible storage.
proposals.security_concerns: The system must not silently read every notification or use microphone content to infer activities. Require per-source enrollment, explicit urgency rules, encrypted queue contents, and a local-only driving/focus signal where possible. Never speak secrets aloud in an interruption; redact or require a button-triggered private review. Sending, deleting, or changing anything remains confirmation-gated.
missing: A cross-surface notification ingestion contract with source-specific permissions and webhooks/polling adapters
A durable urgency taxonomy and owner-editable policy language, including emergency contacts and quiet exceptions
Mac/iOS focus and calendar integrations that expose state without screen scraping
A pendant delivery protocol supporting severity, defer, acknowledgement, and replay receipts
A relay queue schema with deduplication, expiry, redaction, and audit history

proposals.user_asks: Keep a live conversation with me even when LTE-M is congested: prioritize my speech, keep the reply intelligible, and if words were lost, tell me exactly what was missed and resume without making me repeat everything.
proposals.why_useful: The current call can lose nearly eight seconds of the owner's speech when downlink audio overlaps uplink. A coordinated governor lets the pendant, relay, Mac TTS, and browser/action planner degrade gracefully instead of silently dropping intent.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the live speech turn; gpt-5.6-luna on the Mac for post-turn reconstruction/action planning; no model call for packet scheduling or loss metrics.
proposals.latency_budget: Keep local speech priority decisions under 20 ms; target under 250 ms added turn latency. On detected loss, send a brief spoken repair prompt immediately, then let the slower Mac planner reconstruct context in the background.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.00 additional for scheduling/telemetry; occasional reconstruction costs one background gpt-5.6-luna call, dominated by audio transcription/context size. Dashboard telemetry is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio quality metrics and small missing-span transcripts leave the pendant; raw SD fallback remains failure-only and must be encrypted/deleted after delivery. Never execute an inferred browser action without the existing confirmation rules; show uncertainty and packet-loss evidence.
missing: A shared duplex QoS protocol with sequence numbers, playout deadlines, loss reports, and explicit speech-priority mode across nRF9160, Worker, and Mac bridge
Relay support for short repair prompts and resumable audio ranges rather than treating a turn as one opaque stream
A Mac-side reconstruction job that can use transcript/audio gaps and browser context without replaying or duplicating actions
Acceptance tests for intelligibility and loss-repair behavior on congested LTE-M

proposals.user_asks: Give me a genuinely private voice mode: when I say “private note” or flip a hardware privacy switch, the pendant must stop sending raw audio to the cloud, capture locally, and later let the Mac transcribe and file only the text I approve—without exposing the note to browser sessions or relay logs.
proposals.why_useful: Today every live voice turn depends on cloud transport, so a private thought cannot be captured with a trustworthy hardware boundary. This would let the owner use the pendant for sensitive ideas in public or offline, while still turning approved text into a reminder, note, or draft on the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: No cloud model in private capture mode; use a local Mac transcription model in the background, then gpt-5.6-luna only after owner approval to structure or file the text. Realtime is used only outside private mode.
proposals.latency_budget: Hardware mute and local recording indicator must engage within 100 ms. After reconnection, transcription may take 1–2 minutes; filing is explicit and can wait for review.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost until approval; local transcription uses Mac CPU. Optional approved structuring is one background gpt-5.6-luna call, dominated by transcript length.
proposals.security_concerns: Requires a physically enforced mic disconnect or analog mute, not merely a software flag; tamper-evident LED/actuator state; encrypted local storage; relay must receive only opaque delivery metadata; browser extension and dashboard must refuse private-note contents unless the owner explicitly releases them. Destructive or external actions retain confirmation.
missing: A production pendant privacy switch that electrically gates the microphone path and a trustworthy local indicator
On-device encrypted note container with key handling that never sends plaintext to the relay
Mac-local transcription/import protocol with explicit release tokens and browser/dashboard redaction
A testable privacy audit showing no raw audio, transcript, or sensitive filenames leave private mode before approval

proposals.user_asks: “Repeat the last thing you told me, and show me what happened behind it.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable conversation should be recoverable when speech is missed or a job arrives late. The pendant can identify the last interaction even offline; the relay can reconcile its audio and delivery state; the Mac can expose the exact action receipt and browser evidence without making the owner remember a job ID.
proposals.model_tier: deterministic for lookup, reconciliation, and replay selection; background gpt-4.1-mini only to compress a long receipt; realtime only for the new spoken request
proposals.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for last-interaction lookup and a one-sentence replay; under 2 s to assemble cross-surface evidence. No network round trip should be required just to replay the pendant's locally cached last reply.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near $0: D1/R2 and local event joins. A long receipt costs one background gpt-4.1-mini call, roughly a few thousand input tokens; audio replay uses already-rendered PCM where retained.
proposals.security_concerns: Receipts can contain private page titles, mail subjects, or sensitive commands. Keep a sensitivity label with every event, redact by default in spoken output, require explicit confirmation before opening a private browser artifact, and never replay secrets aloud unless the owner asks. Delete cached audio under the configured retention policy.
missing: A stable interaction/attempt ID carried from pendant button press through relay, Mac pipeline, browser command, and final delivery
Terminal pipeline states with append-only delivery acknowledgements instead of runs stuck at processing
A small pendant-side last-reply index with bounded audio metadata and encrypted replay cache
A read-only receipt endpoint and dashboard timeline that joins relay, Mac, and browser evidence

proposals.user_asks: “Privacy hold.” Then, with one more button press, “Resume.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner cannot instantly establish a physical, cross-device privacy boundary. This would make the pendant a trustworthy emergency mute: it would stop microphone capture locally, tell the relay to reject or discard in-flight audio, pause Mac and browser automation, and hold non-urgent notifications until the owner explicitly resumes. The owner gets a clear spoken/LED confirmation when the boundary is active, even if LTE is unavailable.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic firmware and relay state machine; no LLM required. Realtime only handles the owner's spoken “Privacy hold” after local wake, never policy decisions.
proposals.latency_budget: Local microphone shutdown and button confirmation under 100 ms. Relay/Mac/browser revocation under 2 seconds when connected; the pendant must remain safely muted and enforce the hold offline until an explicit resume gesture.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost: state transitions and acknowledgements are deterministic. A small D1 event and dashboard update per transition; no audio upload during the hold.
proposals.security_concerns: This is a security boundary, so fail closed: reboot, LTE loss, malformed commands, and relay failure preserve mute and automation suspension. Do not allow a server push to clear it. Encrypt the persisted state, authenticate resume commands, show the state in the dashboard, and require a physical gesture to resume. Define emergency-alert exceptions explicitly rather than silently bypassing privacy.
missing: A firmware privacy-state machine that gates I2S capture, button semantics, playback, and queued uploads
A signed, monotonic privacy epoch propagated through relay, Mac pipeline, and browser extension so stale commands cannot execute
Relay and Mac/browser middleware that cancels in-flight work and rejects commands from an earlier epoch
A visible dashboard state and audit record for hold/resume transitions
A tested policy for whether safety-critical alerts are suppressed, locally indicated, or allowed through

proposals.user_asks: “Reopen the thing we were working on.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can abandon a task mid-conversation and later resume from the pendant without remembering which tabs, drafts, evidence, or background job were involved. It is more than history: it revalidates stale browser state and reconstructs a safe, reviewable next step across all surfaces.
proposals.model_tier: Use the relay realtime model only for the short spoken request and confirmation; use a cheaper background model to summarize the saved task capsule and compare fresh browser evidence. Mac planner executes reversible workspace restoration; authenticated browser reattaches tabs and refreshes sources; relay coordinates and delivers the result to the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second from the pendant. Restore and freshness-check within 10–20 seconds; if browser or Mac is offline, speak a precise parked-state receipt and retry in the background.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per resume, dominated by background summarization and authenticated-page extraction; realtime cost is limited to two short turns.
proposals.security_concerns: Task capsules may contain private URLs, snippets, drafts, and account metadata. Encrypt at rest, apply sensitivity/TTL fields, redact secrets from spoken summaries, bind browser operations to the original tab/session, and require explicit confirmation before sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting anything. Never replay a stale approval.
missing: A durable cross-surface task-capsule schema containing goal, evidence pointers, open decisions, approvals, expiry, and next action
Relay storage and retrieval keyed to the owner's voice/session identity
Mac endpoint to restore a named workspace and report exactly what changed
Browser freshness validation and provenance-preserving reattachment for authenticated tabs
Pendant-facing resume command and a compact spoken receipt
Dashboard view showing capsule contents, staleness, and pending confirmation

proposals.user_asks: “Capture the last few minutes and turn the decisions into follow-ups.”
proposals.why_useful: After a meeting or hallway conversation, the owner can mark a short audio window from the pendant and receive a sourced, editable follow-up packet instead of trying to remember decisions. The system connects spoken commitments to the relevant Mac workspace and authenticated browser records, while stopping before any external message or calendar change is sent.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to acknowledge the pendant command and confirm the capture boundary. A cheaper background model transcribes and extracts decisions, owners, dates, and uncertainties. Mac planner searches local notes/workspace for project identity; authenticated browser checks matching private records; relay assembles the packet and queues it for spoken or dashboard review.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 1 second. Produce a draft packet in 30–90 seconds after upload. If the Mac or browser is unavailable, retain the marked segment and deliver a partial transcript with explicit missing-source notices.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per capture, dominated by audio transcription and background extraction; browser and Mac work add little model cost but may require several tool calls.
