args.change: Replace the HUZZAH32 classic-Bluetooth audio bridge with a product bridge built around an nRF5340 Audio-class module (LC3/LE Audio, 24 kHz mono path) plus a small fallback classic-A2DP radio if the owner's headphones require it. Keep the nRF9160 for LTE-M/NB-IoT control, but move the 24 kHz packet decode/resampling and jitter buffering off the pendant's overloaded application core. Define a negotiated profile (24 kHz LC3/LE Audio preferred; 16 kHz Opus fallback) and expose packet loss, underrun, and clock-drift counters to the relay.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets intelligible, continuous superwideband speech instead of a 44.1 kHz SBC bottleneck and silence when the bridge buffer starves; older headphones still work through the fallback radio.
args.effort: Medium-high: new bridge PCB/module, antenna and RF coexistence work, LE Audio firmware, headphone interoperability matrix, and an end-to-end audio test fixture. Prototype with an nRF5340 Audio DK before committing to enclosure power design.
args.risk: LE Audio support varies by headphones and the dual-radio design adds pairing complexity; if the preferred path fails, automatically fall back to the existing A2DP path and preserve a wired/local playback test mode. RF coexistence and clock drift can still cause dropouts until soak-tested.
args.cost_impact: Roughly +$18–35 BOM in low volume for the LE Audio module, RF/layout, and fallback radio, plus ~20–60 mA during active playback depending on radio duty cycle; lower pendant CPU load may offset some system power.
args.latency_impact: LC3 framing and jitter buffer target <120 ms mouth-to-ear; profile negotiation adds <1 s only at session start. Removing the current 44.1 kHz resampling/starvation path should reduce sustained underruns.
args.security_impact: New pairing keys and radio firmware increase attack surface; store keys in secure hardware, never send them through the relay, and require explicit user action for pairing/reset.
depends_on: An end-to-end audio acceptance test that measures 24 kHz bandwidth, mouth-to-ear latency, packet loss, and recovery across pendant, relay, and bridge.
Owner decision on whether LE Audio-capable headphones are acceptable or classic-A2DP fallback is mandatory.

args.user_asks: “When I’m listening to a briefing or answer, let me tap the pendant to bookmark the sentence I just heard; later, turn my bookmarks into a cited note with the source and a short follow-up list.”
args.why_useful: A spoken answer often contains one actionable fact that the owner cannot safely remember while walking. A physical tap is faster and more private than dictating a note, and the Mac/browser can attach evidence that the pendant alone cannot reach.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to detect the active utterance boundary and acknowledge the tap; use a cheaper background model on the relay to normalize bookmarks and extract follow-ups. Mac/browser workers fetch source pages and citations, while the dashboard presents an editable note.
args.latency_budget: A local tap acknowledgement under 150 ms; bookmark persistence under 2 s. Citation enrichment may take 10–30 s in the background and must not block listening.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per bookmarked utterance for background transcription/structuring; browser and Mac work dominate wall-clock time, not realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Bookmarks can capture private conversation or logged-in page content. Store the raw audio briefly, encrypt it, attach source URL/tab and timestamp, and require confirmation before sharing or sending any resulting note. Never expose secret page text to public web search.
missing: A pendant-local moment-marker buffer with monotonic audio timestamps and tap debouncing.
A relay API that maps utterance IDs to retained audio/transcript segments and emits a durable receipt.
A Mac/browser citation worker that can re-open the exact source tab and preserve a quoted snippet/hash.
A dashboard review view for editing and confirming the generated note.

args.change: Create a durable cross-surface utterance ledger: relay assigns every spoken turn and generated audio packet a monotonic utteranceId; /pipeline/events records start/end, source references, and playback state; /pipeline/audio carries the same ID; a pendant tap sends a marker against the currently audible ID; Mac/browser enrichment joins only by that ID and writes a receipt containing source URL, timestamp, transcript hash, and note status. Add retention/redaction controls so raw audio can expire while the citation receipt remains.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can tap once and later trust that the note refers to exactly what was heard, even if the Mac reconnects, a job runs in the background, or audio packets arrive out of order. It turns a clever bookmark into a dependable memory aid.
args.effort: Medium: schema and idempotent event API in relay, firmware marker packet, Mac/browser joiner, dashboard review state, and replay tests for disconnects and duplicate packets.
args.risk: Clock drift, reconnects, and late packets may create ambiguous boundaries; use relay-issued IDs, monotonic sequence numbers, explicit unknown state, and never silently guess a citation. If enrichment fails, preserve the raw marker and tell the owner.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage/API overhead per marker; background citation model roughly $0.01–$0.05 each, with raw audio retention configurable to zero after transcript verification.
args.latency_impact: Tap acknowledgement remains local/sub-150 ms; durable ledger write target <2 s after reconnect; enrichment is asynchronous (10–30 s).
args.security_impact: Ledger metadata can reveal listening history. Encrypt at rest, scope source snippets to the owner's authenticated session, redact secrets before model calls, and require confirmation before exporting notes.
depends_on: A pendant-local moment-marker skill (already requested but not yet delivered).
A relay schema and endpoint for utterance markers/receipts.
A browser citation worker that can reattach to the source tab without broadening browser permissions.

transcript.text:
Round 68 findings:

- The pendant currently captures at **15.625 kHz**, uploads Opus at **16 kHz**, and decodes playback at **24 kHz**. Full-duplex Opus consumes about **87% of one application core**.
- The bridge is an **ESP32 classic Bluetooth A2DP source**, locked to **44.1 kHz stereo SBC**. Its buffer starvation has already caused silence.
- The owner’s Mac bridge is online; browser and mobile devices are currently offline.
- The current relay has audio pipeline routes, but no durable cross-surface identity tying together an utterance, its audio packets, a pendant tap, and the eventual citation/note.

I recorded two proposals:

1. **Hardware:** replace or supplement the HUZZAH32 with an LE Audio-capable bridge, retaining classic A2DP fallback where necessary. The proposal was recognized as close to an existing backlog item, so I would not count it as wholly new.
2. **Integration:** build a durable utterance ledger with relay-issued `utteranceId`s, packet sequence numbers, playback state, pendant bookmark markers, source URLs, transcript hashes, and durable receipts. This is the genuinely important missing connective layer.

What I still need:

- An implementation of the **pendant-local moment-marker skill**: debounced tap, local monotonic timestamp, and marker delivery after reconnect.
- A relay endpoint/schema for **utterance markers and receipts**, with idempotency and raw-audio retention/redaction rules.
- A browser citation worker able to reopen the exact authenticated source tab and preserve a quoted snippet/hash.
- A dashboard review state for editing and confirming bookmarked notes.
- The owner’s decision on whether **LE Audio-capable headphones are acceptable**, or whether classic-A2DP compatibility must remain mandatory.
- An end-to-end audio acceptance test covering bandwidth, latency, packet loss, clock drift, reconnects, and bridge underruns.

args.user_asks: “If my connection drops while you’re answering, don’t lose the conversation—resume the exact sentence on whichever surface reconnects first, and tell me if anything was skipped.”

args.change: Add a durable Conversation Media Lease and Handoff Protocol. Every live call gets a sessionId, monotonically increasing media sequence, transcript checkpoint, and current output target (pendant or Mac). The relay monitors bidirectional packet loss, jitter, silence, and websocket age; on a sustained threshold it emits a signed HANDOFF_OFFER containing the last acknowledged sequence and checkpoint. The Mac agent explicitly accepts or rejects, opens local audio, and sends a HANDOFF_ACCEPT. Relay then switches output/input routing without creating a new conversation. On recovery, perform the same lease exchange back to the pendant, discard duplicate frames by sequence, and expose a human-readable receipt in /jobs/:jobId/receipts and the dashboard. Never hand off an action approval itself: only the conversation state moves.

args.risk: False positives could switch audio while the pendant is still usable; use hysteresis and an owner-configured confirmation mode. If Mac audio permission is absent, announce failure on the pendant and continue degraded rather than silently opening another microphone.
args.cost_impact: Negligible inference cost; small durable relay/session storage and telemetry. Mac-side audio capture may require a native helper and modest battery/CPU use.
args.latency_impact: Adds at most 1–2 seconds during a handoff; steady-state media path unchanged.
args.security_impact: Improves security by making endpoint ownership explicit, preventing replay and duplicate approvals. Requires authenticated endpoint keys and short-lived leases; Mac fallback must display an active-mic indicator.

Recorded a new capability: **conversation handoff across surfaces**.

The owner should be able to start a conversation on the pendant, lose connectivity or remove it, and have the Mac, browser, or phone continue seamlessly—then resume on the pendant without duplicate speech or lost context.

To enable it, the system needs:

- A shared session identity and lease across all surfaces.
- Per-device availability and last-heard/playback acknowledgements.
- Relay-controlled output ownership to prevent duplicate delivery.
- Compact transcript/audio checkpoints for exact continuation or brief fallback summaries.
- User controls for permitted fallback surfaces and automatic handoff.

This requires coordination between the pendant, relay, Mac, browser, and dashboard/iOS clients; no single existing surface can provide it alone.

1. **Private-account voice queries without cloud exposure** — the Mac/browser reads authenticated pages locally and returns only approved, redacted fields with an access receipt.
2. **A private-data execution lane** — relay requests are classified as private, raw page content is blocked from cloud paths, and ambiguous requests fail closed unless the owner explicitly approves fallback.

These require field-level sensitivity rules, local typed extraction, signed cross-surface receipts, and robust browser disconnect handling.

args.change: Create a tamper-evident cross-surface execution ledger. At intent creation, assign one traceId and hash-chain events for pendant utterance/gesture, relay plan and jobId, each Mac actionReceipt/actionId, browser commandId/tabId/result, approval checkpoints, audio briefing delivery, and final outcome. Persist only event metadata plus redacted content hashes by default; sign each terminal receipt with the relay key. Add GET /jobs/:jobId/timeline and dashboard/voice rendering that can answer 'what did you do, what evidence proves it, and where did it stop?' across retries and dropped links.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Today Mac receipts and browser command IDs are separate islands: after a long task or a connection drop, the owner cannot reliably distinguish completed work from merely planned work. A single spoken request would yield one concise, auditable completion/failure story with direct evidence and safe retry boundaries, without retaining private page contents or audio unnecessarily.
args.effort: Medium: shared event schema and hash-chain in relay + adapters in local-agent executor/browser bridge + one dashboard timeline view + voice summarizer; roughly 1–2 engineering weeks, then fault-injection tests for duplicate and out-of-order events.
args.risk: Clock skew, retries, or a crashed writer can create gaps; mark gaps explicitly rather than claiming continuity, use idempotent event IDs, and verify chain on read. A compromised Mac could report false receipts, so label events by signer/source and never treat an unsigned client event as proof. Recovery is append-only repair events, not mutation.
args.cost_impact: Small D1 metadata growth (roughly 1–5 KB per action); negligible model cost when queried, with a cheap structured summarizer preferred over realtime. Optional evidence snippets remain opt-in and short-retention.
args.latency_impact: <100 ms per event locally/relay; final spoken summary adds one structured retrieval and can be generated asynchronously for long jobs.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability while reducing data exposure if payloads are hashed/redacted. Requires relay signing-key rotation, per-owner authorization on timeline reads, and explicit separation of secret URLs/content from hashes.

args.user_asks: If I interrupt you or the signal drops, keep my spoken request intact, continue from the last confirmed words, and tell me plainly if anything was lost.
args.why_useful: The current measured LTE-M call loses speech under simultaneous traffic (388 uplink packets, about 7.8 seconds). A wearable conversation that silently drops the owner's words is unsafe for reminders, transactions, and long instructions. This turns loss into a recoverable, honest interaction rather than a guess.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for detecting turn-taking and producing the short recovery prompt; a cheaper background model can reconstruct or summarize buffered segments after the link recovers. Deterministic firmware/relay code should handle sequence numbers, buffering, and loss detection.
args.latency_budget: Normal speech remains realtime. On detected loss, 200–500 ms local acknowledgement ('I missed part of that') and at most 2 seconds to replay/recover a buffered segment; never proceed with an irreversible action until the relevant utterance is confirmed.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental API cost for packet accounting and deterministic recovery; occasional retranscription costs one small background inference. Dominant cost is additional LTE airtime/storage, bounded by a 10–20 second encrypted ring buffer per turn.
args.security_concerns: Audio remains sensitive: encrypt the local ring and relay object, short-retain and delete after confirmed transcription, expose a pendant privacy latch, and require confirmation before any action whose intent was reconstructed. args.risk: A watchdog could close a genuinely slow job prematurely. Use generous timeouts by stage, never infer played from uploaded, and quarantine ambiguous runs for explicit owner review. Recovery is a late event that reopens/reconciles the trace, never deletion.
args.cost_impact: Minimal D1 writes and one scheduled Worker invocation; no extra model call unless the owner asks for a narrative.
args.latency_impact: No hot-path impact; acknowledgements add one tiny control message after playback.
args.security_impact: Delivery metadata is less sensitive than audio, but job IDs and timestamps still require owner authorization. Do not expose raw audio or transcript in watchdog alerts.

args.user_asks: When I walk away from my Mac, keep working on safe preparation, but automatically pause before any private or irreversible step and resume only when my pendant proves I’m back; then give me one spoken handoff of what changed while I was gone.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has no trustworthy boundary between unattended background work and actions that should happen only in their presence. This would let the system make progress without silently sending, purchasing, deleting, or exposing private data while the owner is away, and would make returning to an in-progress task understandable rather than requiring a dashboard hunt.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic policy and cryptographic presence/session checks for pause and resume; use a cheap background model to summarize completed safe preparation. Reserve realtime for the short spoken return handoff and only when the pendant is present.
args.latency_budget: Presence loss should gate the next risky step within 1 second. On return, resume handshake within 2 seconds and produce a concise handoff within 5 seconds. No risky action proceeds during uncertainty or link loss.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost for policy and event handling; one small summarization call per unattended task. Main engineering cost is presence lease, key rotation, and consistent risk classification across Mac and browser.
args.security_concerns: Presence must not be inferred from Wi-Fi or an open browser tab alone. Use a short-lived pendant challenge-response key, invalidate leases on disconnect, and bind approval to the exact action hash. Treat a stolen/unlocked Mac as untrusted; never include private page contents in the return notification until the pendant re-authenticates. Owner-configurable safe-action classes are required.

This requires pendant-backed presence authentication, shared action hashes and risk policy across relay/Mac/browser, resumable checkpoints, and receipt-based handoff summaries.

transcript.text:
Round 76 findings:

- The live path already produces **24 kHz mono PCM** on the Mac and delivers it through the relay.
- The pendant decodes **24 kHz Opus in 60 ms frames**, then resamples to the **31.25 kHz I²S clock** going to the ESP32 bridge.
- Encode and decode together consume roughly **87% of one nRF9160 application core**, making simultaneous conversation and playback vulnerable to underruns.
- The browser device is currently offline; the Mac bridge is online.
- No new entries appear under `granted` this round, so the previously requested tools/contexts do not appear callable yet.

I recorded two new proposals:

1. **“Run a voice quality check.”**  
   A synthetic, end-to-end diagnostic would identify whether problems originate in capture, LTE, relay buffering, Mac TTS, decoding, resampling, or playback. It would produce a short spoken result and a redacted evidence receipt.

2. **Offload audio processing to the ESP32 bridge or a dedicated codec/DSP.**  
   This would reserve the nRF9160 for LTE/session control, reduce playback stutters, and provide headroom for link recovery. The ESP32-only version can be piloted before a hardware revision.

What I still need to complete the 24 kHz path:

- Authoritative **end-to-end audio acceptance thresholds**.
- The **24 kHz target architecture** and compatibility requirements.
- A working `audio_pipeline_validate` tool and fault-injection support.
- The owner’s policy for **interruption, privacy, and resuming queued audio** after a dropped link.
- A measured profile of **nRF9160↔ESP32 transport latency, clock drift, and bridge reset behavior**.

The most important unresolved technical risk is now clear: the relay and Mac can produce the target format, but the pendant’s CPU budget and clock conversion are the likely limiting points.

args.change: Implement a clock-disciplined playback pipeline for the 24 kHz path. Have the ESP32 bridge report monotonic I²S consumption timestamps and ring-buffer fill level; have the nRF9160 use a bounded, high-quality fractional resampler to make sub-parts-per-million corrections toward the measured sink clock instead of assuming a fixed 31,250 Hz rate. Add sequence-aware concealment for one missing 60 ms Opus frame, explicit underrun/overrun counters, and a hard immediate-stop path for the pendant button.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Long replies would keep playing smoothly instead of slowly drifting into a buffer underrun or audible gap because the microphone, modem, nRF clock, and ESP32 I²S clock are not identical. The owner would hear fewer clicks and would still be able to stop speech instantly.
args.effort: Medium-to-high firmware and bridge work: timestamp protocol, resampler tuning, stress tests across temperature and LTE load, and a rollback flag to the current fixed-rate path.
args.risk: An unstable control loop could create pitch modulation or consume excess CPU. Bound correction to a few hundred ppm, update slowly, monitor fill-level variance, and fall back to fixed-rate resampling if the loop becomes unstable. Missing bridge telemetry must not block playback.
args.cost_impact: No model or recurring API cost and no required BOM change. A modest additional CPU cost for fractional resampling; likely lower total cost than repeated retransmission or support diagnostics.
args.latency_impact: No meaningful added conversational latency; maintain a small 60–120 ms playback buffer. Stop remains immediate and out-of-band.
args.security_impact: Only timing and buffer counters cross the local bridge link; no new audio retention or external data exposure. Clear PCM buffers on stop.
depends_on: A measured ESP32 I²S clock and nRF9160 clock-drift characterization
A versioned local nRF↔ESP32 telemetry frame format
24 kHz end-to-end acceptance thresholds

transcript.text:
Recorded a new firmware change:

**Clock-disciplined 24 kHz playback**

The owner should be able to listen to long responses without clicks, drift, or buffer underruns, even though the nRF9160, modem, and ESP32 I²S bridge have independent clocks. The bridge would report playback timestamps and buffer fill; the nRF9160 would make bounded fractional-resampling corrections, conceal an occasional missing frame, and preserve an immediate stop path.

What must change:

- Add timestamp and buffer telemetry between the nRF9160 and ESP32.
- Replace fixed-rate resampling with a bounded adaptive resampler.
- Add sequence-gap concealment and underrun/overrun counters.
- Characterize clock drift under temperature and LTE load.
- Define the 24 kHz acceptance thresholds.
- Keep a safe fallback to the current fixed-rate implementation.

No single node can search and reconcile those private sources with provenance. This capability would return a concise answer plus source-by-source evidence, explicitly marking conflicts and stale material instead of silently blending them.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for indexing and candidate extraction; use the realtime tier only for the owner's spoken query and short answer. A stronger model is reserved for conflict resolution when sources disagree.
args.latency_budget: Answer from the local/private index in 2–4 seconds; if a logged-in page must be opened, speak an immediate progress acknowledgement and finish within 30 seconds. Evidence should remain available for review after the spoken summary.
args.cost_estimate: Indexing is mostly local and incremental. Typical query costs $0.01–$0.04 for reranking and synthesis; authenticated page fetches and conflict resolution dominate. Do not send the full private corpus to the cloud.
args.security_concerns: Build and query indexes on the Mac/relay with per-source sensitivity labels; raw browser content, audio, and secrets stay local unless the owner explicitly authorizes a source. Every claim needs a source locator, capture time, and freshness; exclude secret facts from spoken output by default. Require confirmation before opening a new private site or using a finding to send, delete, purchase, or change anything.
missing: An on-device/private hybrid index spanning Mac workspace files, browser extraction results, relay records, and explicitly retained pendant snippets
A common evidence schema with source locator, capture timestamp, content hash, freshness/expiry, sensitivity, and claim-to-source links

args.change: Create a private, provenance-first evidence graph separate from conversational memory. Mac indexing workers emit file/note metadata and bounded excerpts; the browser bridge emits normalized page regions and locators; relay imports job/pipeline receipts and only pendant snippets explicitly marked retain. Each evidence item gets a content hash, source URI/tab or file locator, capturedAt, lastVerifiedAt, sensitivity, TTL, and deletion tombstone. A claim index stores only links to evidence IDs, never an untraceable model summary. Add source-scoped retrieval, freshness checks, conflict sets, and a citation renderer usable by voice and dashboard. Support rebuild from source adapters after corruption and immediate tombstoning when the owner deletes or revokes a source.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can get a reliable answer from their own scattered information and inspect exactly which file, logged-in tab, job receipt, or retained pendant moment supports it—rather than receiving a confident but unverifiable blend of stale private data.
args.effort: High: local indexing and file-watch adapters, browser extraction contract, receipt import, encrypted vector/keyword indexes, claim provenance storage, deletion propagation, and voice/dashboard citation UX. Requires an explicit retention/consent control for pendant snippets.
args.risk: Indexing can expose sensitive data through embeddings, stale files can be mistaken for current truth, and browser DOM changes can break locators. Discovered this round:

- The Mac bridge is online; the home Chrome bridge is offline.
- The pendant currently has no battery gauge and uses modem/network time only when available.
- Existing job, browser, receipt, event, and audio routes are present, but they are not yet unified into one owner-visible history.
- No new production tools appeared beyond the existing Mac/browser/relay tools.

I recorded two proposals:

1. **Offline catch-up across surfaces** — after reconnect, the pendant says what completed, failed, or still needs approval, combining Mac jobs, browser actions, relay events, and pendant-local events without exposing raw private content.
2. **Hardware support for trustworthy status** — add a low-power fuel gauge and backed-up RTC so the pendant can warn before failure and preserve reliable offline ordering across brownouts and modem restarts.

What I still need—not as another repeated request, but as the remaining blockers—is:

- Authoritative 24 kHz audio acceptance thresholds and production pendant constraints.
- The owner’s definitive phone-companion/privacy boundary.
- A specified reconnect and queued-action resume policy.
- A durable event-envelope implementation connecting existing job, browser, Mac, and pendant receipt writers.
- Firmware support for a reconnect cursor and acknowledgement state.

The key gap is no longer individual routes; it is trustworthy cross-surface continuity when the pendant loses connectivity.

args.user_asks: “Pack what I’ll need for the next few hours onto the pendant so I can ask about it without a connection.”
args.why_useful: Today the pendant becomes largely blind when LTE-M drops. A deliberate offline capsule would let the owner access a small, current subset of their agenda, approved notes, travel details, and selected logged-in page summaries during travel or dead zones, then reconcile harmless annotations after reconnect. This is different from a later catch-up report: it is proactive, owner-chosen context available while offline.
args.model_tier: Background model on the Mac/relay to select and compress requested material; deterministic firmware lookup and small realtime responses offline. No expensive model call for direct indexed retrieval.
args.latency_budget: Build in under 60 seconds for a normal capsule; transfer over the local bridge in under 15 seconds; offline answers should start in under 500 ms.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per pack, dominated by one background summarization pass. Storage is bounded by an owner-selected size cap; no recurring model cost for offline lookup.
args.security_concerns: The capsule contains private calendar, notes, files, or authenticated-page excerpts and must be encrypted at rest with a device-bound key, expire automatically, and support immediate remote revocation on reconnect. The owner must choose categories or approve an automatically suggested manifest. Never cache passwords, payment data, or unrestricted page HTML; show provenance and capture time for every answer.
missing: An encrypted, expiring offline-capsule format and key lifecycle spanning Mac, relay, and pendant SD
Mac/browser exporters that produce redacted records with source URLs, timestamps, and sensitivity labels
A bounded on-device index/query path that fits the pendant’s current RAM and survives power loss
A sync protocol for owner-created offline annotations, with conflict handling and no automatic external side effects
Dashboard controls to inspect, revoke, expire, and erase a capsule

args.change: Introduce an encrypted Offline Capsule protocol: the Mac/browser exporters create a signed manifest of owner-approved, redacted records; the relay issues a short-lived capsule key and version; the pendant stores only the encrypted records plus a compact field index on SD, with an expiry and erase-on-revocation flag. On reconnect, sync only annotations and capsule acknowledgements—never execute actions from capsule data automatically.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave Wi-Fi/LTE coverage with the exact small set of information they chose and still ask the pendant useful questions, without turning the wearable into an uncontrolled copy of their private computer.
args.effort: High: capsule schema and cryptography, browser/Mac export adapters, pendant SD/index/query firmware, bridge transfer, expiry/revocation, and power-loss recovery tests.
args.risk: A stolen pendant or stale capsule could expose private information, and sync conflicts could lose annotations. Mitigate with device-bound encryption, short TTLs, category-level approval, key revocation, signed manifests, atomic SD writes, and read-only offline semantics.
args.cost_impact: Low recurring API cost after packing; modest SD and relay storage. Firmware work is the main cost; no new model call during offline use.
args.latency_impact: Packing is asynchronous; local lookup remains sub-second. Initial transfer may take seconds over the bridge and should show progress.
args.security_impact: Adds a deliberate encrypted data boundary and revocation path, but increases the amount of sensitive data physically present on the pendant. Default to minimal manifests, no secrets/payment data, and automatic expiration.
depends_on: A production pendant key-storage strategy
Mac/browser redaction and provenance exporters
Pendant SD atomic-write and compact-index support
Owner-defined capsule categories, size limit, and expiry

args.user_asks: “If I start talking on the pendant and the task needs my Mac or a logged-in browser, carry the conversation over there without making me repeat myself; show me what will happen, let me approve it from the pendant, and bring the result back as a short spoken receipt.”
args.why_useful: Today the pendant, relay, Mac, and authenticated browser each lose conversational continuity at their boundary. This would make the hive feel like one assistant: the pendant captures intent and approval, the relay preserves state while the Mac/browser work, the Mac opens the right visible context, and the browser supplies private evidence. It is specifically staged and reversible, so the owner never has to approve an opaque remote action or repeat a long explanation.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short spoken handoff/approval and final receipt; use the cheaper background planner for browser extraction and multi-step Mac work, with deterministic typed action execution wherever possible.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge and announce the handoff in under 1 second; show the Mac/browser preview within 3 seconds when online; approval-to-action under 2 seconds; long research or queued work may continue asynchronously and return a receipt later.
args.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn for handoff plus one for receipt (usually <$0.02 total at current voice-tier assumptions); background planning and browser extraction dominate variable cost. No paid model call is needed for typed previews, receipts, or state transitions.
args.security_concerns: Private page content remains on the Mac/browser path and is summarized rather than copied into the pendant unless needed. Destructive actions (send, delete, purchase) remain confirmation-gated; approval tokens are single-use, bound to job/session and expire. The preview must include target account, tab, fields, and evidence timestamps so a stale logged-in tab cannot be mistaken for current state.
missing: A durable cross-surface handoff object: conversation/job ID, intent, evidence, pending approval, and return channel, persisted through relay and Mac restarts.
A pendant-visible preview and approve/cancel protocol (button plus spoken confirmation) that binds approval to a specific action hash.

Mac UI integration that opens/focuses the relevant browser tab or workspace and renders the preview without relying on denied Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions; AppleScript/browser bridge is the fallback.
A result-to-pendant event path with typed receipts and deduplication, including offline/reconnect behavior.

args.user_asks: “Run a quick audio check on the whole system and tell me whether the pendant, LTE link, relay, and Mac can all support a clear conversation right now; if not, say exactly which leg failed and leave a repair record.”
args.why_useful: The current path mixes a 15,625 Hz I2S capture, 16 kHz/16 kbps Opus uplink, LTE-M bursts, a practically half-duplex link, relay storage, and Mac pipeline endpoints. A local-looking 'it sounds bad' complaint currently cannot distinguish microphone, clock/sample-rate conversion, radio loss, relay backpressure, or playback. A coordinated probe would make the 24 kHz path shippable and let the owner know whether to charge, move location, reconnect the bridge, or wait for repair instead of repeatedly retrying voice.
args.model_tier: No realtime model for measurement; use deterministic firmware/relay/Mac probes. Use a cheap background model only to turn measurements and logs into a short diagnosis and repair checklist.
args.latency_budget: A 5–10 second test with a spoken result under 15 seconds; a failed leg should be identified within one round trip. Persist raw samples/metrics asynchronously, not in the voice prompt.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; one short LTE test burst and temporary audio objects. Storage cost is minimized by retaining metrics and a short waveform excerpt only when a threshold fails, with automatic deletion after the configured retention.
args.security_concerns: The test must use synthetic tones or locally generated phrases, never upload ambient room audio without an explicit start. Mark diagnostic recordings separately from conversation recordings, encrypt/authenticate the report, and provide a one-command purge. Do not expose network identifiers or raw UART logs in the spoken result.
missing: A versioned audio probe protocol spanning pendant/ESP32 bridge, relay, and Mac with sequence numbers, timestamps, sample-rate/codec declarations, packet-loss/jitter/underrun metrics, and pass thresholds.
A server/Mac endpoint that runs the probe and correlates all four legs into one incident ID and repair receipt.
A firmware test mode that can generate/recognize a synthetic loopback tone while the one-button conversation state is idle.
A 24 kHz acceptance profile and downgrade report (24 kHz, then 16 kHz fallback) rather than a single binary pass/fail.

args.change: Add an end-to-end audio-contract and diagnostic correlator between pendant firmware, ESP32 bridge, relay, and Mac. On an explicit test request it assigns one incidentId and monotonically numbered synthetic frames; each hop reports declared sample rate/codec, capture/playback timestamps, packet loss, jitter, queue depth, underruns, and LTE reconnects. The relay joins the reports and emits a typed pass/degrade/fail receipt with a 24 kHz result and a 16 kHz fallback result. It stores metrics by default and only a short synthetic waveform excerpt on failure; all records carry an expiry.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When audio is unclear, the owner gets a precise answer—microphone, clock conversion, radio, relay, or Mac—instead of guesswork and repeated failed conversations. It directly provides the acceptance evidence needed to finish the 24 kHz path without uploading ambient speech.
args.effort: Medium: define a small protocol and thresholds, implement firmware/bridge counters and synthetic loopback, add relay correlation and a Mac diagnostic route, then exercise loss/reconnect cases. No Accessibility or Screen Recording permission is needed.
args.risk: Incorrect thresholds could label a usable link degraded, or a probe could contend with a live conversation. Require explicit start, reserve a short test window, tag every frame with a probe ID, and abort on button press. If a component drops out, the correlator returns partial evidence rather than claiming pass; expire raw excerpts automatically.
args.cost_impact: Near-zero model/API cost. Small LTE test payload and a few D1/R2 writes per diagnostic; bounded retention keeps storage predictable. Firmware RAM impact is limited to counters and a small synthetic-frame ring buffer, not full speech buffering.
args.latency_impact: Adds an explicit 5–10 second diagnostic only when requested; normal conversations are unchanged. Correlation is asynchronous and the spoken summary can arrive as soon as the first complete leg reports.
args.security_impact: Synthetic audio only by default; authenticated incident IDs prevent mixing reports from different tests. Raw excerpts are opt-in/failure-only and short-lived. The report should redact device identifiers from the spoken result while retaining them for local repair logs.
depends_on: A versioned 24 kHz acceptance profile and thresholds (currently requested context is still outstanding).
A firmware/bridge test-mode hook that can generate and recognize synthetic audio without Accessibility.
A durable diagnostic receipt/index so the owner can ask what failed later (incident diagnostics and catch-up status requests remain outstanding).

transcript.summary: I discovered the live capabilities, owner constraints, hardware, and backlog, then recorded two genuinely cross-surface proposals and an integration change. New work: an explicit pendant→bridge→LTE-M→relay→Mac audio conformance test that uses synthetic frames, correlates packet loss/jitter/underruns and sample-rate negotiation under one incident ID, and returns a 24 kHz/16 kHz fallback receipt. I also proposed a spoken task handoff, but the recorder correctly flagged that as close to existing continuity work; the useful missing connective pieces are durable handoff state, single-use approval binding, and reconnect-safe return receipts.

args.user_asks: “Give me a private, searchable timeline of what the pendant heard, what the Mac or browser did, and what actually changed—with the source evidence for each step—and let me export or erase any day.”
args.why_useful: The owner can currently obtain isolated job receipts, logs, browser evidence, and audio objects, but cannot reconstruct one trustworthy story across a spoken request, delegated work, authenticated tabs, and the resulting world change. A unified, owner-controlled timeline would make the system auditable, debuggable, and portable: they could answer “what did you do yesterday?”, verify a claim, or erase sensitive history without trusting an opaque database.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic indexing, hashes, and typed joins for the timeline; use a cheap background model only for optional natural-language labels and clustering. Realtime is unnecessary except for a short spoken answer when the owner asks from the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Recent-day queries should render in under 2 seconds and a spoken answer in under 4 seconds. Large exports can run as background jobs and return a completion receipt; erasure should report completion only after every surface confirms deletion.
args.cost_estimate: Low ongoing model cost because indexing and joins are deterministic. Storage and export cost dominate: retain compact metadata and evidence hashes by default, with raw audio/page captures separately opt-in and expiring.
args.security_concerns: This is more sensitive than ordinary logs because it joins private speech, browser sessions, and actions. Encrypt exports, keep them local by default, redact secrets and tokens, require explicit confirmation for exporting raw audio or page text, and make deletion cryptographically auditable without retaining the deleted content. Never expose the owner's captured secret fact in search results unless explicitly requested.
missing: A canonical event schema and correlation ID shared by pendant utterances, relay turns, Mac jobs, browser commands, receipts, and external mutations.
A durable provenance index that can join those events without copying private page contents into every surface.
Owner-facing search/export/erase APIs and a dashboard view with per-event source, timestamp, confidence, retention, and deletion status.
A deletion fan-out protocol covering D1/R2, Mac workspace/logs, browser evidence, and any pendant/SD diagnostic cache, with verification receipts.

args.change: Create a privacy-scoped, append-only event ledger that assigns one correlation ID at the pendant utterance and links relay turns, audio object hashes, Mac job/action receipts, browser tab evidence, and final external-state observations. Store typed metadata and content hashes centrally, keep raw speech/page text at its originating surface with independent TTLs, and expose a verified export/erase fan-out that reports which surfaces acknowledged deletion.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one dependable answer to “what happened?” instead of manually reconciling unrelated logs, and can take the record with them or remove a sensitive day without deleting blind spots or leaving hidden copies.
args.effort: High: define schema and retention policy, add correlation propagation to firmware/relay/Mac/browser, implement a local-first index and export format, then build deletion acknowledgements and failure recovery across online/offline surfaces.
args.risk: A join bug could associate one person's private browser evidence with another task, or erasure could falsely claim success. Use owner-scoped authenticated IDs, immutable event hashes, explicit partial/deletion-pending states, and never treat missing acknowledgements as deleted. Keep raw content out of the central ledger by default.
args.cost_impact: Low model cost; metadata/index writes are modest. Export and temporary encrypted bundles consume storage, while raw audio/page evidence remains bounded by existing retention controls.
args.latency_impact: No meaningful impact on live voice if events are buffered asynchronously; recent timeline queries should be a fast indexed read. Export/erase of large histories is background work.
args.security_impact: Substantially improves auditability but creates a high-value metadata target. Encrypt at rest and in transit, minimize content, isolate per-surface keys, require confirmation for raw-content export, and make the owner's erase action stronger than ordinary undo.
depends_on: A canonical cross-surface event schema and propagation hooks, which do not exist as one contract today.
A durable deletion fan-out/acknowledgement mechanism across relay D1/R2, Mac workspace, browser evidence, and pendant SD.
An owner-facing timeline/search/export/erase surface.

args.user_asks: “While I’m away from my Mac, capture this thought on the pendant; when the Mac is reachable, file it into my AI-Pendant-Workspace with the time, location-free provenance, and a short searchable title, then tell me exactly where it went.”
args.why_useful: This is a genuinely wearable-to-desktop workflow: the pendant is the only always-with-owner capture surface, the relay can hold it while the Mac sleeps or the LTE-M link drops, and the Mac is the only node that can safely organize the workspace. It turns fleeting spoken thoughts into durable, reviewable notes without pretending the pendant can run filesystem automation.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the initial short capture confirmation and title suggestion; a cheaper background model should normalize/transcribe and classify the note, while the Mac agent performs deterministic file creation. No browser or expensive realtime turn is needed after capture.
args.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 500 ms with a local receipt; relay durable acceptance under 2 s when connected; filing may wait until the Mac reconnects and should normally complete within 1 minute. If the link is unavailable, preserve the capture and say it is queued rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per note depending on audio transcription/model use; storage and relay invocations dominate only at high volume. Mac filing is local and free.
args.security_concerns: Voice content leaves the pendant over LTE-M to the relay unless an offline-only mode is selected. Do not infer or store location. Workspace writes are reversible but should use atomic create-with-unique-id and receipts; never overwrite an existing note. Any secret-like content needs sensitivity marking and should not be echoed in spoken confirmation. Mac filesystem access remains bounded to ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace.
missing: A durable pendant capture spool with sequence numbers and retry/ack semantics
A relay note-ingest endpoint that returns an immutable receipt and deduplicates retries
A Mac-side workspace filing action with atomic writes and a completion receipt
A compact transcription/title pipeline and a user-visible queued/ filed state
An explicit retention and deletion policy for captured audio versus derived text

args.change: Add an append-only capture-to-action ledger shared by pendant, relay, and Mac. Each voice capture or requested action gets a monotonic device sequence, relay receipt, SHA-256 payload hash, current owner-visible state (captured, uploaded, transcribed, filed, failed), and parent/child links when one capture creates multiple Mac/browser actions. Retries must reuse the same event ID; the Mac filer commits its filesystem write and receipt in an idempotent outbox transaction. Expose a compact reconciliation endpoint so reconnecting pendants and the dashboard can show the first missing state rather than replaying or claiming completion.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops wondering whether a spoken note or computer action happened twice, vanished during LTE-M loss, or was filed without confirmation. A single short receipt can say exactly what was accepted and what remains queued, even after a crash or reconnect.
args.effort: Medium-high: protocol schema and migration, relay durable store, small firmware sequence/ack changes, Mac outbox/reconciliation, and failure-injection tests across reconnect and power loss.
args.risk: A schema or clock mistake could strand events or create false completion. Recover with append-only records, versioned envelopes, bounded replay, and a repair command that never performs an irreversible action. Filesystem writes remain temp-file-plus-rename and duplicate-safe.
args.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; modest relay durable-storage and log volume (small metadata per event, audio retained separately under an explicit TTL).
args.latency_impact: One metadata acknowledgement adds tens of milliseconds on a live path; filing latency is unchanged except during reconciliation. Audio payloads should not wait for the full ledger commit before local acknowledgement.
args.security_impact: Hashes provide integrity, not secrecy. Encrypt sensitive payload metadata at rest, redact spoken text from general logs, and keep the ledger scoped to the owner's bearer identity. Never put secret note contents in dashboard URLs or spoken receipts.
depends_on: A durable capture spool and relay note-ingest contract (not yet granted)
A Mac workspace filing action with atomic receipt (not yet granted)
A documented retention policy for raw audio and derived text
Existing /pipeline/events, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and Mac action receipt infrastructure

Round 81 findings:

- The orchestrator has not exposed any new grants this round; `granted` is empty.
- The pendant remains a prototype nRF9160 DK with 211,608 B application RAM.
- Current audio is asymmetric: 15.625 kHz microphone capture and 16 kHz/16 kbps uplink, but 24 kHz playback. Opus encode/decode already consumes roughly 87% of one core.

- The durable browser job runner is still incomplete: routing exists, but persistence, retries, job IDs, and result streaming are missing.
- Existing action receipts and job routes are present, but there is no single cross-surface ledger connecting pendant capture, relay acceptance, Mac filing, and final owner-visible state.

I recorded two proposals:

1. **Capture thoughts on the pendant and file them into `~/AI-Pendant-Workspace` later**, with queued/filed receipts and no false success claims.
2. **An append-only capture-to-action ledger** using device sequence numbers, deduplicated event IDs, hashes, state transitions, and reconciliation after reconnects or crashes.

What is still needed to make the first capability real:

- Durable pendant capture spool and retry/ack protocol.
- Relay note-ingest endpoint with idempotent receipts.
- Mac workspace filing action with atomic, duplicate-safe writes.
- Background transcription/title generation.
- Explicit raw-audio and derived-text retention policy.
- The pending 24 kHz audio acceptance criteria and validation tooling.
- A durable browser job runner and result stream for long-running authenticated work.

I did not re-request the already-denied macOS permissions or the capabilities still awaiting orchestration.

args.change: Design the production pendant with a hardware-backed device identity and tamper-evident capture path: a secure element for per-device keys and monotonic counters, encrypted external QSPI storage for a bounded local event journal, and a physical privacy circuit that cuts microphone power independently of firmware. Bind every uploaded audio/event envelope to the secure-element signature and counter; the relay rejects cloned or replayed envelopes and the owner can revoke one pendant without rotating the whole fleet.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust that a spoken thought or approval came from the pendant they are actually wearing, survives a dropped connection without silently disappearing, and is truly private when the mute control is engaged—even if firmware crashes or the relay account is compromised.
args.effort: High: select and qualify a secure element and QSPI part, redesign the pendant PCB and power domains, add manufacturing provisioning and revocation service, implement encrypted journal wear-leveling and signed envelopes, and validate recovery under brownouts and flash failure.
args.risk: Added parts and provisioning complexity could make units harder to manufacture; flash wear or a lost key could strand queued captures. Recover with bounded ring storage, key escrow only for device replacement (never plaintext audio), signed firmware migrations, and a factory reset that explicitly destroys the old identity.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 additional BOM per unit, plus provisioning/revocation infrastructure; QSPI adds a few milliamps only during writes, while the secure element's standby draw is negligible. No per-request model cost.
args.latency_impact: Signature generation and journal commit add tens of milliseconds to event acknowledgement, but the pendant can acknowledge locally before LTE-M upload. Microphone mute is immediate in hardware.
args.security_impact: Substantially improves authenticity, replay resistance, and local privacy. It creates a high-value device key, so provisioning, revocation, backup, and physical teardown procedures must be treated as security-critical. Encrypted storage protects queued content at rest but does not replace retention controls.
depends_on: A versioned signed event-envelope protocol shared by firmware and relay
Relay-side device enrollment, revocation, and replay-counter validation
The product pendant hardware replacing the current nRF9160 DK prototype
A documented policy for queued audio retention and device replacement

args.cost_estimate: A few cents per captured thread at most; most future matches are local string/entity comparisons. Relay storage is small metadata plus a short owner-approved excerpt, not continuous audio.
args.security_concerns: Do not retain raw microphone audio by default. Store sensitivity, source, timestamp, and an encrypted short transcript; never copy authenticated page contents to the relay. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say an idea once while walking and reliably get it back at the moment it becomes useful, without recurring alerts, cloud surveillance of browsing, or having to remember which note contained it.
args.effort: Medium: event adapters for frontmost app/browser tabs, local index and matcher, lifecycle/expiry store, relay receipt, and pendant acknowledgement UX; add tests for private windows, duplicate tab transitions, and app crashes.
args.risk: A false match could interrupt the owner or reveal a sensitive reminder on a shared screen. Start opt-in, require high confidence, suppress in private windows and during focus modes, rate-limit resurfacing, and provide immediate snooze/delete. args.cost_impact: Near-zero ongoing API cost; deterministic local matching handles normal cases. Occasional background embedding or semantic disambiguation can stay below $0.01 per bookmark. Storage is a few KB per bookmark and event hash.
args.latency_impact: Local event matching is sub-second; relay/pendant delivery adds network latency only when the owner has opted into spoken resurfacing.

I discovered and recorded a concrete new gap, based on live evidence:

- The browser is online, but one `browser_navigate` idempotency key failed **6/6 times**.
- A different navigation key succeeded **7/7 times**.
- There are currently **7 pending browser commands**.

This is not a general browser outage; blindly retrying the same command is the problem.

I proposed:

1. **Evidence-driven browser circuit breaker**
   - Stop identical retries after two failures.
   - Distinguish timeout, tab disconnect, navigation error, and authentication block.
   - Capture the last confirmed URL, tab/session, DOM hash, and evidence capsule.
   - Try at most one safe, read-only alternate backend.
   - Never automatically repeat a mutation.

2. **Pendant-led resumable recovery**
   - The pendant says exactly where the job stopped.
   - The relay stores a durable checkpoint.
   - The Mac/browser resumes from the last confirmed step.
   - A write or submission always requires explicit approval.

I also informed `mac-terminal` of the observed failure pattern and proposal.

What is still needed to build this fully:

- A durable checkpoint schema linking relay job, browser request, tab/session, evidence, and next step.
- The failure classifier and circuit-breaker implementation.
- A strict public-versus-private policy for deciding whether Browser Run may be used as a fallback.
- A pendant event/approval protocol for **resume**, **abandon**, or **take over**.
- The owner’s final policy for whether a recovered **read-only** action may proceed automatically; mutation retries should remain confirmation-gated.

args.user_asks: When you are unsure which of my open tabs, accounts, or Mac documents I mean, ask me one short disambiguating question on the pendant with the two concrete choices, then continue without making me repeat the whole task.
args.why_useful: Today ambiguity is resolved by whichever surface happens to answer first, or by sending a long task back to the planner. The owner should be able to resolve identity while away from the screen: the browser contributes candidate tabs and evidence, the Mac contributes document/app candidates, the relay reduces them to a safe choice, and the pendant captures the owner's answer. This prevents acting on the wrong private account or document without requiring a desktop session.

args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 second; return a compact correction within 10 seconds for up to three sources. Longer investigations become a durable job and notify the pendant when complete.

args.security_concerns: Evidence may include private browser pages, files, or sensitive memories. Keep source access authenticated per surface, redact citations on shared displays, retain an audit trail, and require explicit approval before changing durable memory or taking any external action.

args.latency_budget: A local loss decision in under 300 ms; replay/acknowledgement within 2 s after reconnect; no more than one recovery prompt spoken aloud.

args.cost_impact: Small relay D1/R2 metadata and temporary audio overhead; occasional duplicate realtime transcription. Firmware needs flash wear budgeting, not necessarily new silicon. Exact cost depends on replay volume.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms local buffering/ACK behavior and typically 1–2 s recovery after reconnect; normal connected turns should be unchanged.

- The Mac bridge is online; the browser session is offline.

I recorded two proposals:

1. **Recoverable conversations:** sequence-numbered audio, server acknowledgements, a bounded pendant replay buffer, deduplication after reconnect, and a truthful recovery receipt when speech was lost.
2. **Production audio hardware:** separate modem and audio/DSP domains, a real 24-kHz microphone path, DMA-based buffering, and hardware privacy muting. The current development kit is not sufficient for reliable superwideband duplex audio.

What I still need is implementation and validation rather than more discovery:

- The pending 24-kHz architecture and acceptance thresholds.
- Link-aware duplex audio control and fault injection.
- A durable local audio checkpoint/replay buffer.
- Idempotency gates so a replayed transcript cannot repeat an action.
- Incident diagnostics and delivery receipts.
- A production pendant specification beyond the nRF9160 DK.
- The owner’s final privacy, interruption, and queued-action-resume policies.

I will not re-request those because they are already queued.

args.user_asks: “Pause everything you’re doing, preserve exactly where you are, and tell me what is safe to resume.”
args.why_useful: Today a long-running Mac or browser workflow can outlive the owner's attention, but there is no single spoken, cross-surface pause barrier. The owner needs to be able to interrupt from the pendant while the relay, Mac planner, and browser bridge atomically stop issuing new work, preserve the current step and evidence, and report whether anything was already committed. This is different from undo: it prevents the next action and makes the handoff understandable before resuming.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to recognize and acknowledge the short interruption; use a cheaper background model to summarize checkpoints and classify resumable versus committed steps.
args.latency_budget: The pendant acknowledgement should arrive within 500 ms. New Mac/browser actions must be blocked within 1 s; checkpoint summarization may take up to 5 s.
args.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus an inexpensive checkpoint summarization. Storage is small structured state and evidence metadata; raw screenshots or page text should be retained only under the existing job retention policy.
args.security_concerns: The pause command must be authenticated to the active owner session and take precedence over queued work. It must not falsely claim that an already-submitted external transaction was stopped. Every surface needs an append-only barrier event, action sequence number, and receipt; resuming an irreversible step requires explicit confirmation.
missing: A cross-surface pause barrier with monotonically ordered action epochs
Mac and browser adapters that check the barrier immediately before every side effect
A checkpoint schema containing current step, precondition, evidence, committed status, and safe resume point
A pendant spoken acknowledgement that distinguishes halted, in-flight, and already-committed work

args.change: Add a cross-surface action-epoch lease to the job protocol. Every relay-dispatched Mac or browser side effect carries {jobId, epoch, stepId, preconditionHash}; the relay can atomically advance the epoch to PAUSED. Mac and browser bridges reject stale epochs before execution, while in-flight operations report an outcome of not-started, started-not-confirmed, or committed. Persist a checkpoint and evidence pointer for each transition, then expose one spoken/dashboard receipt.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can stop a workflow from the pendant without racing the Mac or browser. They get a precise answer about what happened, rather than an unreliable cancellation message or a need to reconstruct state from logs.
args.effort: Medium: shared protocol and D1 schema, bridge preflight checks, job-worker integration, and race-condition tests with delayed browser and shell actions.
args.risk: A pause arriving after an external site accepts a request cannot undo that request; the receipt must say so. A stale client could otherwise execute after pause, so fail closed on missing or expired epochs and require a fresh lease to resume.
args.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; a few durable metadata writes per action and modest dashboard storage. No new hardware required.
args.latency_impact: One lightweight preflight/lease check per side effect, targeting under 50 ms locally and under 200 ms through the relay; pause propagation under 1 s.
args.security_impact: Improves containment by making pause authoritative and auditable. Epoch tokens must be unguessable, scoped to the authenticated owner session, and never treated as proof that an external transaction was reversible.
depends_on: A durable job runner that honors cancellation
Browser request IDs and tab/session affinity
The existing job receipt and undo records
A shared action idempotency gate

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability and integration change:

**Owner capability:**  
“Pause everything you’re doing, preserve exactly where you are, and tell me what is safe to resume.”

This would give the pendant an authoritative stop command across the relay, Mac, and browser—not merely an undo. The system would halt new side effects, preserve the exact checkpoint, and distinguish:

- not started,
- started but unconfirmed,
- already committed,
- safe to resume.

To support it, the stack needs a cross-surface action-epoch lease, pre-execution checks in the Mac and browser bridges, durable checkpoints with evidence, and explicit spoken/dashboard receipts. Irreversible external actions would still require confirmation after resumption.

The relay can continue while the Mac is unattended, the browser can retain the owner’s private session, and the pendant can provide a physical, low-ambiguity approval without requiring the owner to reopen a screen. It must refuse if the staged page, values, scope, or risk changed.
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for planning, extraction, and change detection; use realtime only to explain the final receipt over audio. Deterministic policy code, not a model, validates the approval token and exact before/after hash.
args.latency_budget: Background work may take minutes. The review notification should reach the pendant within 2 seconds of staging; approval acknowledgement within 1 second when LTE-M is available, with a spoken fallback if the link is interrupted.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per background task depending on browser/model calls; approval and receipt are negligible. Dominant cost is authenticated page extraction and long-running planner context.
args.security_concerns: Never transmit page secrets into the spoken prompt or store them in the approval payload. Bind a short-lived, single-use token to session/tab, URL, action type, normalized before/after values, risk class, and expiry. A second press cancels; changed DOM, stale session, timeout, reconnect, or any destructive/send/purchase action requires fresh review. The pendant LED should indicate staged versus approved without exposing content.

A pendant-side single-use approval/cancel gesture and signed acknowledgment (the one-button hardware needs a deliberate long-press or press-confirm sequence)
A server policy gate that revalidates the exact staged record immediately before execution
Push delivery and retry semantics to the pendant, including a safe expired-token state

args.change: Add a low-power I2C fuel-gauge IC and a small vibration/ haptic actuator to the production pendant, with firmware exposing battery percentage, estimated runtime under LTE-M transmit, and charge/thermal fault events. args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant should not silently die during a conversation or halfway through a browser transaction. The owner gets an early spoken warning, a reliable checkpoint, and a chance to charge before losing work; haptics also provide private confirmation in noisy or public settings.
args.effort: Moderate hardware spin plus fuel-gauge driver, calibration, health telemetry schema, relay policy, and Mac/dashboard notifications. Validate across cold starts, USB power transitions, LTE bursts, and a depleted cell.
args.risk: Incorrect state-of-charge estimates could cause premature pauses or missed shutdowns; mitigate with conservative voltage/current calibration, hysteresis, and explicit unknown state. A new I2C device can interfere with future peripherals; reserve its address and add bus recovery. If the gauge fails, fall back to voltage/USB presence and mark confidence low.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$4 BOM increase for gauge, haptic motor, driver, and assembly; haptic adds brief 10–30 mA pulses, while the gauge is typically tens of µA. No meaningful model/API cost; telemetry is small.
args.latency_impact: Health samples every 30–60 seconds, with immediate event reports on low-battery thresholds. No impact on audio loop except a tiny telemetry frame.
args.security_impact: Battery and fault telemetry is low sensitivity but should be device-authenticated; do not include location or raw identifiers in spoken warnings. Signed snapshots prevent a stale Mac health report from authorizing risky continuation.
depends_on: A production pendant design rather than the current nRF9160 DK prototype
A device-health endpoint/event schema in the relay
Queued-action resume policy and link-aware audio governor
Owner-configurable thresholds for warning, checkpoint, and hard stop

args.security_concerns: Classify event sensitivity before speech: never speak message bodies, account names, or browser secrets in public mode. Critical actions remain review-only and cannot be triggered by an interruption.

args.model_tier: background for transcript cleanup, project classification, and indexing; realtime only for the initial spoken acknowledgement
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge locally/streaming in under 1 second; save and enrich the note within 5 seconds. Retrieval should be a deterministic indexed lookup, escalating to the planner only when the project reference is ambiguous.
args.cost_estimate: Typically one short background inference (roughly 500–1,500 input tokens) per capture and none for exact retrieval; dominant costs are transcription and optional browser-context extraction, not the realtime acknowledgement.
args.security_concerns: The captured audio/transcript and surrounding page title/URL may be sensitive. args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and background inference cost; avoid realtime calls after acknowledgement. A small local index and bounded audio retention are the main operational costs.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second acknowledgement; enrichment is asynchronous and normally completes in under 5 seconds. Retrieval is local/deterministic for known project ids.
args.security_impact: Sensitive content stays on the relay/Mac path, with field-level redaction and bounded retention. Never transmit full authenticated page bodies by default; store URL/title and a hash or owner-selected excerpt.

args.risk: Over-redaction could make tasks fail; under-redaction is a privacy incident. Recover by preserving the original only on the Mac, offering a narrowly scoped owner-approved retry for one region, and versioning every decision for audit.
args.cost_impact: Small local CPU/memory overhead; negligible API cost when deterministic detectors suffice. Occasional ambiguous classification adds a low background-model cost.
args.latency_impact: Usually below 150 ms locally; screenshot OCR and ambiguous classification may add seconds and should be skipped or fail closed in realtime.
args.security_impact: Materially reduces secret exfiltration risk, but must itself avoid logging raw payloads, protect policy configuration, and treat redaction manifests as potentially sensitive metadata.

args.user_asks: For the next hour, handle routine incoming requests for me within rules I say out loud—triage them, draft replies, and suggest calendar changes—then bring me only exceptions or anything that would commit me.
args.why_useful: The owner gets temporary, bounded delegation instead of either micromanaging every notification or granting an unsafe permanent automation. The worn pendant defines the scope and expiry; the relay keeps working if the Mac sleeps; Mac and private browser sessions inspect the owner’s actual accounts; the owner approves only exceptions and commitments.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for classification, rule matching, and draft preparation. Use realtime only to capture the spoken delegation scope and answer exception questions. Use the local Mac/browser agents for authenticated reads and reversible draft/calendar preparation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the delegation locally in under 2 seconds. Process routine arrivals asynchronously within a few minutes; surface urgent exceptions within 30 seconds when the link is available. Never wait for model completion before enforcing the expiry locally at the relay.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.05 per hour-long delegation window, dominated by periodic authenticated-page/message extraction and draft generation; simple rule checks and expiry are nearly free.
args.security_concerns: The spoken scope must compile into an explicit allowlist (people, accounts, actions, time window, spending/calendar limits), shown on the dashboard and summarized back by audio. Never send, purchase, delete, accept an invitation, or make a binding commitment automatically. Store drafts and evidence encrypted with short retention; revoke immediately on a second button press or spoken stop; reject stale or changed page state. Private browser content must stay on the Mac/browser bridge and relay should receive only normalized fields needed for triage.
missing: A capability-lease primitive shared by relay, Mac, and browser, with monotonic expiry, revocation, and an auditable scope hash
An event intake connector for new Mail/Messages/calendar/browser notifications that can wake the relay without polling every page
A policy compiler that turns spoken limits into typed action classes and routes uncertain items to an exception queue
Owner-defined defaults for who counts as routine, acceptable calendar moves, quiet hours, and escalation urgency

args.change: Introduce a signed, append-only Capability Lease protocol. A lease contains principal, allowed surfaces, typed action classes, resource/account selectors, spending/time limits, expiry, revocation counter, and scope hash. The relay validates every Mac/browser job and pendant-originated request against the lease; agents attach the lease ID and scope hash to every receipt; any mutation of scope or revocation invalidates outstanding work atomically.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can safely say “you may handle these routine things until 5” and trust that the permission really ends, even if a job is still queued, the Mac reconnects later, or a browser tab changes. It gives them an understandable audit trail instead of hidden standing access.
args.effort: Implement D1 lease and revocation tables, signed tokens, middleware in /plan, /execute, browser command submission, and job workers, then add pendant start/stop/expiry UX and receipt display. Add crash/reconnect and clock-skew tests across relay and Mac bridge.
args.risk: A validator bug could over-authorize or strand legitimate work. Default deny, short leases, monotonic server expiry, an emergency global revoke, and compatibility mode that permits read-only status but no mutations provide recovery. Key rotation and replay protection are required.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1 reads/writes per job and roughly 1–3 KB metadata per lease/receipt. Engineering effort is substantial because all action ingress paths must share the validator.
args.latency_impact: Approximately 5–20 ms for a cached lease check; a cold D1 check may add under 100 ms. No extra model latency.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves least privilege and auditability, but introduces signing keys and a high-value authorization validator. Keep private page content out of leases, rotate keys, bind leases to authenticated owner/device identities, and log denials without sensitive payloads.
depends_on: A typed policy/action taxonomy shared by Mac and browser harnesses
A durable relay event/job identity and receipt linkage
Pendant-local stop/revoke handling that works during a dropped LTE link

transcript.text:
Recorded two new proposals:

1. **Time-bounded delegation windows** — the owner can say, “Handle routine requests for the next hour,” with explicit limits, automatic expiry, exception escalation, and approval required for commitments.

2. **Signed Capability Lease protocol** — a relay-level authorization layer enforcing each delegation’s scope, account limits, expiry, revocation, and audit trail across the pendant, Mac, browser, and queued jobs.

These require a shared typed policy system, durable lease/revocation storage, event intake for incoming work, and pendant-local cancellation that remains effective during link loss.

args.user_asks: “Mark this for later.” Capture the exact moment across my pendant, Mac screen, and active browser tab, then bring it back when I return to that project or page—showing what I saw, what I said, and why I marked it, without me having to remember where it came from.
args.why_useful: People lose the reasoning behind half-finished work, not just the URL. A durable, privacy-preserving context bookmark would let the owner leave a thought while walking away and recover it at the right computer context days later. This is more than a note or task: it preserves the multimodal state and reconnects it to the project when the owner returns.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to extract entities, project/page fingerprints, and a concise explanation; use realtime only to acknowledge the mark and answer a later spoken retrieval request.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the mark in under 1 second; snapshot and indexing may finish within 10 seconds. Resurfacing should appear within 3 seconds of a matching project/page context.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.003–$0.02 per mark and resurfacing, dominated by screenshot/audio transcription and embedding; use local hashing and short transcripts to minimize cloud tokens.
args.security_concerns: Screen captures, browser URLs, and voice may contain secrets. Encrypt the packet, redact password/payment fields, keep raw audio/screenshots on the Mac by default, upload only hashes and extracted text unless explicitly enabled, and provide one-button deletion. Never use a mark as authorization for a later external action.
missing: A cross-surface context-bookmark record linking a timestamped pendant utterance, Mac visual state, browser tab/session, active project, and semantic fingerprint
A local Mac capture path that can take a screen/window snapshot without Accessibility and a browser extension payload that can provide DOM/title/URL context
A privacy/redaction pipeline for screenshots, audio transcripts, and logged-in page data
A context-match trigger that can resurface bookmarks on project/page return without interrupting the owner at unrelated times

args.change: Create a signed cross-surface context-epoch stream. The Mac agent emits an epoch whenever the active project, window, or browser tab meaningfully changes; the browser extension contributes a sanitized page fingerprint; the pendant contributes only an explicit mark ID and timestamp. The relay joins these events into a bookmark packet and evaluates matches when a later epoch resembles the marked one. Keep raw screen/audio local and transmit only signed IDs, fingerprints, and owner-approved excerpts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Returning to a project would automatically restore the reasoning and evidence attached to the exact moment they left, even if the original tab moved or the Mac restarted. It turns scattered unfinished work into something recoverable without surveillance or a cloud copy of the owner's screen.
args.effort: Medium-high: event schema and signatures, Mac/browser epoch emitters, local packet storage, relay matching, restart/replay handling, and a deletion/export surface.
args.risk: A weak fingerprint could resurface an irrelevant or sensitive bookmark. Require confidence thresholds, show the source context before interrupting, expire unmatched packets, and allow the owner to disable capture globally or per app/site. Signed sequence numbers prevent replay and duplicate marks.
args.cost_impact: Small background storage and embedding cost; raw artifacts remain local, so cloud egress is low. No new per-invocation realtime spend.
args.latency_impact: Negligible event overhead; matching can run asynchronously and notify only after a high-confidence return context.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy versus uploading ambient state, but signed fingerprints can still reveal project names. Encrypt at rest, scope keys per device, omit sensitive domains by default, and make deletion cryptographically complete across relay and Mac.
depends_on: A local context-bookmark packet format and retention policy
Browser extension support for sanitized tab fingerprints
Mac active-project/window observation that works without Accessibility where possible
Relay replay protection and device-key provisioning
An owner-visible review/delete interface
