args.user_asks: “Finish the checkout I started in Safari, but do not submit until I approve it on the pendant.” Then, after I hold the approval button, submit exactly the staged order and tell me what happened.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful cross-surface action: the pendant supplies deliberate consent, the browser supplies the authenticated checkout session, the Mac executes only the bound plan, and the relay preserves the handoff if one surface drops. It prevents both silent no-ops and accidental purchases.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the short spoken summary and confirmation readback; deterministic planner/executor for checkout inspection and submission; background model only for extracting a concise receipt from page evidence.
args.latency_budget: Stage in under 5 s; physical approval should be reflected in under 2 s; submit and receipt in under 10 s. If any surface is offline, retain the staged plan rather than retrying a purchase.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per invocation, dominated by one planner/readback pass; browser inspection and deterministic execution dominate latency, not model tokens.
args.security_concerns: Never send card numbers or page secrets to the relay/model. Bind a plan digest, target tab/session, merchant, amount, cart hash, expiry, and world fingerprint; require the pendant nonce and reject any page or price change. Store redacted receipts, not checkout contents. Submission, messages, and other irreversible actions require the physical approval; cancellation must be possible before expiry.
missing: Relay persistence and delivery for the existing physical_transaction_approval_latch staged nonce; the approval readback path is currently not completable.
A browser transaction adapter that exposes merchant/cart/total as typed fields and refuses unbound navigation.
A real submit-and-receipt coordinator joining browser result, Mac job receipt, and pendant approval; existing approval currently has no production caller.
Orchestrator closeLedger and relay job leases before safe outage recovery can be enabled.

args.user_asks: “Show me every fact you inferred about me from the last week, and forget this one everywhere.”
args.why_useful: The system currently extracts facts into facts/context structures that the owner cannot inspect or erase. This makes memory trustworthy: each item is shown with its source and derived copies, and deletion covers local graph, extracted facts, evidence capsules, and replicated relay copies while preserving action audit history.
args.model_tier: Background model to cluster and explain candidate facts; deterministic code for provenance traversal, deletion tombstones, and verification; realtime only to read a short result aloud.
args.latency_budget: List in under 3 s locally; deletion acknowledgement in under 5 s; off-machine erasure may be pending and must be reported as such, never claimed complete.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.02 per list/delete request; storage traversal and replication dominate, with model cost limited to human-readable explanations.
args.security_concerns: Require exact item selection and confirmation before deletion. Show evidence text minimally and redact sensitive fields. Delete the extracted fact, derived graph nodes/edges, and evidence capsule—not job history—then issue an off-machine pending receipt for relay/D1/R2 copies. Keep an immutable deletion audit event without retaining the erased content.
missing: A provenance index linking each extracted fact to evidence capsules, context-graph entities/relations, facts.json entries, and relay replicas.
Typed list/delete routes with tombstone propagation and a read-only post-delete verifier.
Dashboard and pendant presentation for recognisable fact summaries; opaque IDs alone are not sufficient for consent.
A retention worker that resolves requested-and-pending off-machine erasures and reports convergence.

args.user_asks: “Is this browser page safe to act on? Read the relevant details to me, identify what would change or be sent, and do not click anything.”
args.why_useful: A wearable owner can get a compact, non-mutating safety review of an authenticated page without handing control to an opaque model. It makes the browser useful for high-consequence decisions while preserving the physical approval boundary for any later action.
args.model_tier: Background model extracts and summarizes page claims; deterministic browser inspection and redaction enforce the target-tab binding; realtime model speaks only the final short assessment.
args.latency_budget: Snapshot and spoken answer in 3–6 s. Never wait indefinitely for a browser bridge; return a stale/unknown verdict with timestamp and tab identity.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.005–$0.03 per review, dominated by page extraction and one summarization pass.
args.security_concerns: Read-only by construction: no click, type, navigation, or submit actions. Bind to an exact tab/session and capture timestamp; redact passwords, tokens, payment fields, and unrelated tabs. Clearly label model inference versus page evidence and require a separate staged transaction flow for any action.
missing: A typed browser-inspection route returning page title, origin, forms, outbound destinations, monetary totals, and destructive controls without raw secrets.
A provenance-preserving risk schema with evidence spans and freshness timestamps.
Pendant speech/UI for uncertainty and a one-tap path to stage (not execute) a reviewed action.
Browser identity attestation remains unavailable, so tab binding must use the existing session/URL constraints until that grant exists.

args.user_asks: “Before you submit anything from my browser, read me the exact fields and destinations that will be sent, compare them with what I approved, and stop if even one changed.”
args.why_useful: A merchant total can remain unchanged while the address, subscription flag, recipient, or outbound destination changes. This gives the owner a concrete, spoken diff at the last responsible moment, rather than trusting a stale screenshot or a generic approval nonce.
args.model_tier: Deterministic extraction and canonicalization for form fields, origin, destination, and amount; background model only converts the diff to plain speech; realtime tier reads the final diff and refusal.
args.latency_budget: Final diff within 2 s of the submit attempt. If the browser cannot be inspected in that window, fail closed and preserve the staged action for a later conversation.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.003–$0.02 per check; browser snapshot and hashing dominate, with little model work.
args.security_concerns: Never transmit raw secrets or full form values when a redacted hash suffices. Canonicalize and hash approved fields at staging, bind to tab/session/origin, and invalidate on navigation, DOM replacement, origin change, price/address/recipient change, or expiry. A mismatch must be a hard stop, not a warning the model can override. Keep an append-only redacted diff receipt.
missing: A browser-side typed form extractor and canonical field allowlist; current inspect/result surfaces are too unstructured for a security comparison.
A stable tab/session identity attestation (the already-requested browser_identity_attestation remains unresolved).
A submit interception point that performs the comparison immediately before mutation, not merely when the plan is created.
Relay storage for the approved canonical digest and a pendant speech/LED refusal state.

args.change: Implement the missing durable approval handoff and guarded browser-transaction coordinator: persist staged plan digest/world fingerprint/expiry and pendant nonce in relay storage, deliver the readback on the next conversation, reject stale or changed browser state, and join the final browser result to the Mac job receipt. Add relay job leases and close ordinary ledgers so outage recovery cannot mistake every historical plan for an interrupted one.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A deliberate hold on the pendant would become real consent instead of an audit-only signal, and a dropped Mac or browser would fail closed without duplicating a purchase or leaving the owner with a promise that nothing can finish.
args.effort: Medium-high: relay schema/store changes, coordinator state machine, browser typed extraction, integration tests, and hardware-in-the-loop approval tests.
args.risk: A bug could block legitimate actions or, worse, submit against stale state. Recover by defaulting to refusal, preserving the staged plan for explicit restaging, and requiring digest/world/nonce matches at the final mutation boundary.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and API cost per staged action; one small D1 row and a few receipts. Model cost remains limited to spoken summaries.
args.latency_impact: Adds ~0.5–2 s for final state verification; no impact on ordinary read-only browser work.
args.security_impact: Improves security by making approval action-bound, expiring, replay-resistant, and fail-closed. Secrets stay in the browser/Mac; relay stores hashes and redacted metadata only.
depends_on: Implement the APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT rather than its current schema-only documentation.
Wire physical_transaction_approval_latch delivery and next-conversation readback; unprompted pendant push is unavailable.
Add typed browser form extraction and the unresolved browser identity attestation.
Fix orchestrator closeLedger calls and add relay job lease_until/requeue before enabling resume.

args.finding: The granted audio_link_fault_inject capability is not callable against the live inventory: its 5% SWB fault test resolved to nothing, with nearest real routes GET /audio-retention and POST /pipeline/audio. The audio validator also requires an explicit pipeline ID and did not run when omitted.
args.evidence: audio_link_fault_inject returned resolution=unresolved; audio_pipeline_validate returned invoked=false, why pipelineId required.

transcript.text:
Round 248 produced four recorded proposals:

1. **Pendant-approved browser checkout** — stage an authenticated transaction, require a physical pendant hold, submit only the unchanged plan, and return a joined browser/Mac/relay receipt.
2. **Last-moment outbound-field diff** — immediately before submission, compare approved versus current form fields, destinations, recipient, address, and amount; fail closed on any change.
3. **Read-only browser safety review** — summarize what a page would send or change without clicking, typing, navigating, or exposing secrets.
4. **Relay implementation change** — make the existing approval latch operational with durable approval state, next-conversation delivery, expiry, replay protection, browser world fingerprints, job leases, and proper ledger closure.

The extracted-fact deletion proposal was rejected as a duplicate of the existing “show and forget inferred facts everywhere” capability, so I did not rephrase it.

### What I still need

- **Relay approval implementation:** the approval-handoff contract is documented but not actually persisted or delivered in production. Until this exists, a pendant approval cannot safely authorize a browser action.
- **Typed browser form extraction:** `/browser/inspect` and browser results are too unstructured for a security-grade comparison of amount, recipient, address, destination, and subscription state.
- **Browser identity attestation:** still unresolved. Until granted, tab binding must rely on weaker URL/session constraints.
- **Final mutation hook:** the browser executor needs an interception point immediately before submit, where the digest and world fingerprint are checked again.
- **Resume prerequisites:** ordinary orchestrator ledgers must be closed correctly, and relay jobs need expiry/requeue leases before automatic recovery is safe.
- **Audio fault testing:** the granted `audio_link_fault_inject` tool currently does not resolve against the live inventory. My attempted SWB test did not run. The validator also requires an explicit pipeline ID; omitting it only produced a dry resolution.
- **Owner policy:** the mandatory-confirmation policy for external actions remains outstanding. I did not re-request it because it is already queued.

args.user_asks: “Lock down every surface now: mute the pendant, stop capture, cancel queued browser/Mac actions, revoke browser command leases, and tell me which surfaces are actually converged.”
args.why_useful: The existing privacy latch protects the pendant, but it does not prove that browser commands, queued Mac work, or relay-held actions have stopped. One emergency command would give the owner a real cross-surface panic boundary instead of assuming local silence means system-wide privacy.
args.model_tier: Deterministic state transition and receipt verification; realtime model only speaks the short convergence result.
args.latency_budget: Local pendant mute immediately; relay and Mac cancellation within 3 s; convergence receipt within 5 s. If a surface is unreachable, report it explicitly as unconfirmed and keep the lock latched.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per invocation; dominated by receipt fan-out and health checks, not model inference.
args.security_concerns: The lock must be fail-closed and idempotent, cancel only commands owned by this device/session, revoke browser leases without deleting audit history, and never claim convergence from a timeout. Clearing the lock requires a deliberate local action plus a fresh authenticated session.
missing: A cross-surface emergency-lock state machine and authenticated convergence receipt.
Relay-side cancellation/revocation primitives for queued and processing jobs.
Browser command invalidation that the extension enforces before executing a polled command.
Mac executor cancellation for currently running work, with explicit non-cancellable states.

args.user_asks: “Read the one-time code currently visible in my authenticated browser and speak it to me through the pendant, without sending the code to the relay, model, logs, or clipboard.”
args.why_useful: The owner can complete 2FA and other sensitive workflows hands-free without copying a secret into a general-purpose model or leaving it in browser history, clipboard state, relay storage, or job receipts.
args.model_tier: Local deterministic OCR/extraction on the Mac; no cloud model and no relay persistence. Realtime audio only transports the already-redacted, ephemeral speech result over the authenticated local path.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 s from request to spoken code; secret buffer erased immediately after playback or a 30-second timeout.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; local OCR and short-lived encrypted IPC dominate.
args.security_concerns: Bind extraction to the explicitly selected authenticated tab, never expose raw pixels or code to the relay, disable clipboard and logging, redact screenshots and receipts, erase buffers on completion, and require a physical pendant hold before speaking a detected secret. If tab identity or local transport cannot be authenticated, refuse.
missing: A local-only browser secret extraction route with strict field types and no raw-page forwarding.
An authenticated Mac-to-pendant ephemeral secret channel; current browser and relay paths are not designed for secret delivery.
Browser identity attestation, which remains unresolved.
A firmware playback mode that marks secret audio as non-recordable and emits no durable transcript.

args.user_asks: “Hand this conversation to my Mac exactly where we left off, but show me the sentence, task state, and pending decision you are carrying before you continue.”
args.why_useful: The owner should be able to move between the worn pendant and the Mac without losing the active thread or silently inheriting stale assumptions. A previewed, bounded handoff makes continuity visible and lets the owner reject incorrect context before any action resumes.
args.model_tier: Deterministic handoff packaging and state diff; background model summarizes only the conversation excerpt and pending decision; realtime model handles the spoken preview.
args.latency_budget: Preview in 2 s and handoff in 5 s. No action resumes until the owner accepts the presented handoff.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.005–$0.02 per handoff; storage and state comparison dominate.
args.security_concerns: Include only the selected conversation, never ambient history. Bind the handoff to session, device, and expiry; show pending irreversible actions separately; require explicit acceptance before rehydrating context or dispatching work. Preserve an audit receipt without retaining rejected context longer than its TTL.
missing: A user-visible handoff envelope containing transcript excerpt, active goal, pending actions, source timestamps, and expiry.
A pendant-to-Mac presentation/acceptance protocol independent of the unavailable unprompted push path.
A context diff verifier that distinguishes new owner input from stale recovered state.
Integration with existing workbench handoff records without turning them into automatic action resume.

args.user_asks: “Only let this Mac and browser act while my pendant is physically present; if the link disappears, freeze sensitive commands and show me exactly what was blocked when it returns.”
args.why_useful: A stolen, unattended, or merely unlocked Mac should not retain the ability to perform sensitive browser actions. Presence would become a bounded authorization condition, while ordinary observation can continue in degraded mode and queued work is frozen rather than silently replayed.
args.model_tier: Deterministic lease and command gate; realtime model only explains blocked and released work.
args.latency_budget: Suspend sensitive command dispatch within one lease interval (under 5 s); restore only after authenticated reappearance and explicit owner policy. No model round trip belongs in the security decision.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; small authenticated heartbeat/lease traffic and bounded relay state.
args.security_concerns: Presence is not identity by itself: bind the pendant key, session, and lease; use monotonic counters and replay rejection; distinguish link loss from deliberate privacy latch; never auto-submit commands accumulated during absence. Non-sensitive reads may remain available only if the owner configures that mode.
missing: A cryptographic pendant presence lease and key provisioning path.
Mac and browser executor gates that classify commands as presence-required and freeze them before dispatch.
Relay lease expiry/reconciliation and a durable blocked-command receipt.
An owner policy for which action risk tiers require physical presence versus per-action approval.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Ephemeral browser-secret delivery:** read a one-time code locally from the authenticated browser and speak it through the pendant without sending it to the relay/model, clipboard, logs, or persistent storage. Requires local-only extraction, browser identity attestation, an authenticated Mac–pendant secret channel, and non-recordable firmware playback.

- **Previewed pendant-to-Mac conversation handoff:** show the owner the exact carried sentence, active goal, pending decision, and expiry before continuing on the Mac. Requires a user-visible handoff envelope, pendant acceptance path, context diff verification, and explicit acceptance before any action resumes.

- **Pendant-presence authorization lease:** freeze sensitive Mac/browser commands when the pendant disappears and report what was blocked when it returns. Requires cryptographic presence leases, executor gates, relay expiry/reconciliation, and owner-configurable risk tiers.

The emergency “stop everything everywhere” idea was rejected as already present in the backlog, so I did not restate it.

args.user_asks: “What changed across my browser, Mac, and pendant since I last checked, and what actually needs my attention?”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has to ask separate surfaces and cannot distinguish a new event from a stale job or a browser result that never completed. This produces one bounded, provenance-linked delta digest: Mac jobs and receipts, authenticated browser changes in explicitly bound tabs, relay delivery state, and pendant inbox/approval state, with each item labeled observed/failed/pending and a direct next action. It is the single most useful daily capability because it turns the hive from a set of tools into a trustworthy continuity layer.
args.model_tier: background for collection and deterministic diffing; realtime only to summarize on demand
args.latency_budget: Initial digest under 5 s from cached snapshots; fresh browser probes may take up to 20 s and must be explicitly labeled live
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.04 per digest; browser probes and model summarization dominate, while receipts and hashes are local/deterministic
args.security_concerns: Only inspect browser tabs/session bindings the owner explicitly authorizes; never include page credentials or raw private DOM by default. Every item needs source, timestamp, and evidence receipt; mutation is never implied by the digest.
missing: A durable cross-surface cursor/watermark per owner acknowledgement
Typed delta normalization joining relay jobs, Mac jobs, browser results, and pendant inbox records
A dashboard/pendant presentation for grouped pending/failed/changed items

args.user_asks: “Before I open or download this, tell me whether it is the same file/page I trusted before, what changed, and quarantine it if it is not.”
args.why_useful: A logged-in browser and Mac can reach private documents that the pendant cannot inspect, while the relay can retain a compact provenance record. This capability gives the owner a practical safety boundary against changed invoices, attachments, and look-alike pages: compare origin, signed/cryptographic identity where available, content fingerprint, and prior owner-approved evidence, then stage—not silently perform—a quarantine or move when the identity drifts.
args.model_tier: deterministic hashing and policy checks first; background model only for explaining semantic differences
args.latency_budget: 2–5 s for known local files/pages; up to 15 s for an authenticated page extraction; no download or move without confirmation
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.02 per check; hashing and metadata are cheap, semantic diff is the main variable
args.security_concerns: Never upload file contents by default; hash locally and send only redacted metadata/diff spans. Browser extraction must be restricted to an owner-bound tab. Quarantine is a write and requires the existing physical_transaction_approval_latch or equivalent explicit confirmation.
missing: A typed file/page identity capsule with canonical URL, origin, size, hash, signer and prior-approval reference
A safe local quarantine action with receipt and undo semantics
Browser extension support for owner-visible, redacted semantic diff regions

args.user_asks: “I’m about to leave—make sure nothing private is still recording, queued, exposed in the browser, or waiting for approval, and tell me exactly what remains.”
args.why_useful: The current privacy latch can stop the pendant, but the owner has no single end-of-session assurance across relay persistence, Mac jobs, browser exposure, queued captures, and staged transactions. This capability performs a read-only convergence audit, separates stopped/contained from pending/off-machine, and offers only explicitly confirmed cleanup actions. It is the practical privacy boundary for a wearable that spans devices.
args.model_tier: deterministic state convergence and receipts; realtime speech only for the short owner-facing result
args.latency_budget: Under 3 s from cached leases; up to 10 s for live browser/Mac checks; must return partial results rather than hang
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per audit; dominated by live bridge/browser checks, not model tokens
args.security_concerns: The audit itself must not expose captured audio or page contents. Report opaque IDs, counts, timestamps, and retention state. Cleanup of off-machine copies is asynchronous and must say requested/pending. Any deletion or cancellation requires confirmation and a durable receipt.
missing: A unified end-of-session state machine tying privacy latch state to relay queues, Mac capture/jobs, browser sessions, and approval records
A typed cleanup plan distinguishing stop, cancel, delete, and await-replication
Owner-facing presentation of partial convergence and stale-device warnings

args.change: Add a cross-surface causal timeline protocol. Each relay, Mac, browser-extension, and pendant event carries its local monotonic counter plus wall-clock observation, boot/session epoch, source, and predecessor receipt. The relay stores only compact event headers and computes a bounded partial order with explicit uncertainty intervals instead of pretending the clocks agree. Expose causal links such as staged→approved→dispatched→browser-applied→audio-delivered and mark gaps or impossible reversals.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When something goes wrong, the owner can hear the truth about what happened and in what order—rather than a misleading list of timestamps. It makes “it said it sent it, but I never heard it” and “the page changed before/after I approved” answerable across devices.
args.effort: Medium-high: event schema, boot/session handling on pendant and bridge, relay partial-order reducer, and adapters for existing job/browser/audio receipts.
args.risk: Clock mistakes or duplicate events could create false causal links. Preserve raw source events, never delete them during reduction, and label uncertain ordering. Roll out read-only first and compare against known audio/job traces.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and API cost: roughly 100–300 bytes per event header; no model cost for ordering.
args.latency_impact: Negligible on hot paths if reduction is asynchronous; a fresh explanation may wait 1–3 seconds for late receipts.
args.security_impact: Event headers can contain sensitive URL/job labels, so encrypt or redact payload labels and bind access to the owner token. Never include page contents or audio in the timeline.
depends_on: A typed shared receipt/event envelope across existing Mac, browser, relay, and pendant producers
A durable owner acknowledgement cursor for reading the timeline
Existing audio_delivery_ack_queue and action/job receipts must expose stable predecessor IDs

transcript.text:
This round I added three owner-facing capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface “what needs my attention?” digest**  
   Combines fresh Mac jobs, browser changes, relay receipts, pendant inbox state, and pending approvals into one short, provenance-linked answer.

2. **Trust-before-open/download check**  
   Compares a file or authenticated page against its previously trusted identity, reports meaningful changes, and can stage quarantine with explicit physical approval.

3. **Leaving-home privacy convergence check**  
   Verifies that capture, playback, relay persistence, Mac jobs, browser exposure, and staged approvals are stopped or clearly marked pending.

I also proposed a **cross-surface causal timeline** so the system can explain ordering—staged → approved → dispatched → applied → delivered—without pretending independent device clocks are exact.

What I still need to make these real:

- A typed shared event/receipt envelope with source-local counters, session epochs, predecessor IDs, and uncertainty intervals.
- A durable owner acknowledgement cursor so “since I last checked” is reliable.
- Browser identity capsules containing canonical URL/origin, content hash, signer metadata where available, and redacted semantic differences.
- A safe Mac quarantine action with receipt and undo behavior.
- A unified convergence state machine distinguishing stopped, contained, pending, stale, and deletion-requested.
- A clear owner policy for browser tab/session scope and whether “I’m leaving” should merely report pending work or also stage cancellation.
- The previously requested mandatory-confirmation policy context remains unresolved; I did not re-request it.

args.user_asks: “Before I send or say this, tell me whether it reveals something private about me, who could receive it, and what safer wording keeps the useful part.”
args.why_useful: The system can already see owner-authored context on the Mac, authenticated browser sessions, and extracted personal facts, but it cannot act as a disclosure boundary. This would catch accidental oversharing in email, messages, forms, and spoken replies while preserving the owner's intent. It would report the exact evidence behind a warning and never rewrite or send without confirmation.
args.model_tier: background classification and deterministic policy checks; realtime only for the short spoken warning
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for text already in the conversation; up to 8 seconds when inspecting a bound browser form or recipient context
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.05 per assessment; semantic classification dominates
args.security_concerns: The analyzer itself must not broaden access: inspect only owner-selected drafts or explicitly bound form fields, redact secrets before model use, and retain only a hash plus decision receipt. Sending, typing, or changing text requires explicit confirmation.
missing: A privacy taxonomy for facts, recipients, and disclosure purposes
Recipient/context extraction from bound Mail, Messages, and browser sessions
A redacted explanation format that cites the relevant fact without repeating the secret

args.user_asks: “Find contradictions in what my calendar, reminders, browser pages, and recent conversations say, and ask me only about conflicts that change what I should do.”
args.why_useful: The hive currently stores observations in separate systems and can act on stale or mutually inconsistent information. A contradiction service would compare dates, commitments, names, and status claims across explicitly authorized sources, rank conflicts by consequence, and present one concise clarification question instead of silently choosing a source.
args.model_tier: deterministic normalization and temporal comparison first; background model for entity resolution and concise questions
args.latency_budget: 15 seconds for an on-demand sweep; under 3 seconds for cached recent sources
args.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.08 per sweep; source reads and entity-resolution inference dominate
args.security_concerns: Only compare sources the owner binds for that request. Store conflict fingerprints and source pointers, not full calendar, page, or conversation contents. Never edit a source while resolving a contradiction.
missing: A common fact representation with source authority, observed time, effective time, and confidence
Connectors that expose bounded Calendar, Reminders, browser, and conversation evidence
A conflict lifecycle: open, owner-resolved, superseded, and intentionally ignored

args.user_asks: “I replaced or reset my pendant. Restore my privacy settings, pending inbox, and safe operating policy without restoring old audio or granting the new device authority by accident.”
args.why_useful: A wearable can be lost, reset, or replaced. Today the owner cannot safely migrate the state that matters—privacy latch policy, transport preferences, pending non-audio inbox items, approval trust, and delivery cursors—without either starting over or risking stale authority. This would make replacement survivable while explicitly excluding recordings and requiring a fresh physical binding ceremony.
args.model_tier: deterministic manifest migration and cryptographic verification; background model only to explain differences
args.latency_budget: 5–15 minutes for a deliberate replacement ceremony, with every stage resumable
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 per migration; cryptographic operations and small relay metadata dominate
args.security_concerns: The old device must be revoked before the new one receives authority. Never migrate audio, raw transcripts, browser secrets, or approval tokens. Require possession of the old device where possible plus a physical approval on the new one; provide a signed recovery receipt.
missing: Device identity and revocation records in the relay
A versioned, allowlisted pendant-state manifest with per-field sensitivity
A two-device or recovery-key binding ceremony and replay-resistant migration receipt

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

- **Disclosure guard** — before sending or saying something, identify private facts, recipient exposure, and safer wording without transmitting or modifying anything automatically.
- **Contradiction resolver** — compare authorized calendar, reminders, browser, and conversation evidence; surface only conflicts that materially affect what the owner should do.
- **Pendant replacement ceremony** — migrate privacy policy, safe settings, pending non-audio inbox state, and delivery cursors to a replacement device without migrating recordings, secrets, or stale authority.

They require, respectively:

- A privacy taxonomy, bounded recipient/form inspection, and redacted evidence explanations.
- A common fact model with source authority and effective time, plus bounded connectors and a conflict lifecycle.
- Relay device identity/revocation, an allowlisted state manifest, and a two-device or recovery-key physical binding ceremony.

args.user_asks: When I say “do this,” stage the risky action, tell me what is waiting, and let me approve it with the pendant’s physical button; then carry it out exactly once and tell me what happened—even if the Mac or relay restarted.
args.why_useful: This closes the currently broken approval promise and makes the pendant a real consent boundary: the owner can approve a browser/Mac action without trusting an invisible software flag, and a crash cannot silently turn an approval into a duplicate action.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the spoken summary and confirmation; deterministic relay/Mac code for digest, nonce, lease, execution, and receipts; background model optional for explaining the result.
args.latency_budget: Stage acknowledgement under 1 s; physical approval reflected within one reconnect/heartbeat (normally under 2 s); execution status within 5 s for local actions. No action runs before the approval receipt is verified.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per invocation when the spoken summary uses a small realtime turn; deterministic storage and receipt work dominate neither latency nor cost.
args.security_concerns: The pendant receives only an opaque transaction nonce and digest, never page contents or secrets. Bind approval to plan digest, world fingerprint, expiry, and monotonic anti-replay counter; require a fresh physical approval for off-machine, irreversible, or unrepeatable steps. Surface refused/expired/world-moved outcomes rather than retrying.
missing: Implement relay persistence for the existing APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT and deliver the pending frame on the owner’s next conversation (the pendant cannot be interrupted out of band).
Connect POST /prepare to the planner and POST /approve to the physical_transaction_approval_latch event.
Give the execution a durable workbench context and a single final receipt joined to the approval nonce.

args.user_asks: Show me every fact you inferred about me, where it came from, and let me delete one fact everywhere you stored it—without deleting my action history.
args.why_useful: The system currently extracts facts into facts.json/context graph that the owner cannot inspect or individually erase. This turns hidden memory into an accountable, owner-controlled surface while preserving the audit trail of actions the system actually took.
args.model_tier: Background model for extraction summaries and human-readable evidence labels; deterministic code for listing, dependency traversal, deletion tombstones, and receipts.
args.latency_budget: List under 2 s locally; deletion acknowledgement under 2 s with a clearly marked pending state for relay replicas; convergence check in the background and reported later.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per list/delete in normal use; storage/index updates dominate, not model tokens.
args.security_concerns: Redact unrelated evidence and expose only the owner’s extracted facts. Deletion must remove the fact, derived graph copies, and its evidence capsule, but retain job history unless separately requested. Off-machine deletion is reported requested-and-pending, never falsely completed; use an idempotency key and signed deletion receipt.
missing: A typed owner-facing facts endpoint with stable fact IDs, provenance capsules, and dependency edges (not just raw context-graph entities).
A cross-store erase worker for local files, context graph, relay D1/R2 replicas, plus a convergence receipt.
A dashboard/voice presentation that distinguishes extracted fact from task/reminder data and supports one-item confirmation.

args.change: Add a lease_until/lease_owner to relay_jobs, requeue expired processing jobs, and make every Mac execution carry an idempotency key tied to its workbench context. Also make the orchestrator close its action ledger on terminal success/failure, then run a startup reconciliation that only resumes steps whose replaySafety is idempotent/additive and whose lease is still valid; all other steps become owner-visible 'needs approval' rather than replaying.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A Mac sleep, browser disconnect, or relay restart will no longer leave work stuck for 24 hours or duplicate an unrepeatable action such as sending a message, while safe file/status work can recover without making the owner start over.
args.effort: Medium-high: schema migration and sweep worker, executor idempotency plumbing, ledger close calls, and crash/restart integration tests across browser and Mac jobs.
args.risk: A lease race could cause two workers to contend; enforce compare-and-set claims and idempotent receipts, and default ambiguous/inflight/unrepeatable steps to blocked. Reconciliation must be dry-run logged before enabling automatic safe resumes.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and worker CPU; one small D1 update per claim/heartbeat and periodic sweep. No model cost.
args.latency_impact: Normal jobs gain one claim/receipt write; recovery begins on the next sweep (target under 30 s) instead of waiting for TTL pruning.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by narrowing replay to explicit replaySafety and retaining approval for risky steps. Does not grant new authority; it should preserve the existing single-token limitation until a separate authorization boundary exists.
depends_on: Use the existing actionLedger replaySafety/riskTier classification rather than inventing a reversibility vocabulary.
Wire the existing workbenchTransaction commit/retry engine into production execution.
Add integration tests for browser command lease expiry and Mac crash between inflight record and receipt.

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: Am I private right now? Check the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser and answer plainly whether any microphone capture, playback, queued audio, relay persistence, or browser exposure is still active.
args.why_useful: The physical privacy latch is local and immediate, but the owner currently has no trustworthy cross-surface answer about convergence. This gives a single spoken truth check after a latch press or whenever privacy matters, without pretending a local LED proves the relay and browser have stopped.
args.model_tier: Deterministic checks and authenticated receipts first; realtime model only translates the structured verdict into a short spoken answer. Never use the model to infer safety from missing evidence.
args.latency_budget: Local latch state immediately; full cross-surface verdict under 3 s when links are healthy. If a surface is unreachable, answer UNKNOWN with the exact stale/missing surface rather than SAFE.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for structured verdicts; under $0.01 only when a natural-language explanation is needed.
args.security_concerns: The check is read-only and must authenticate each surface’s receipt, include freshness timestamps and latch ID, and distinguish stopped from unobserved. Do not expose audio contents or browser page contents. A failed check should offer the owner the existing local latch, but must not silently mutate state.
missing: A pendant-signed latch state receipt and a relay receipt that includes queued-audio/persistence state.
A browser bridge query for capture/playback exposure and a Mac query for active audio jobs, joined by latchId.
Owner-facing stale-data policy and a compact LED/voice vocabulary for SAFE, UNKNOWN, and NOT_PRIVATE.

args.user_asks: Before you use a logged-in website for me, tell me exactly which account and tab you are about to use, prove that it is the intended session, and refuse if the tab identity or destination changed.
args.why_useful: A browser action can be aimed at the wrong logged-in account or a changed tab while still returning a plausible success. This gives the owner a concrete session-boundary check before private or consequential browser work, without requiring page contents to leave the machine.
args.model_tier: Deterministic tab/session attestation and URL/origin checks; realtime model only summarizes the attestation and asks for confirmation when policy requires it.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms for a cached attestation and under 2 s for a fresh browser snapshot. Refuse closed, navigated, duplicated, or stale tabs instead of retrying against another tab.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.005 per check; browser snapshot and signed receipt dominate, with no model call for routine checks.
args.security_concerns: Return opaque account/session identifiers and origin, not cookies, tokens, or page secrets. Bind the attestation to commandId, tab/session ID, origin pattern, and expiry; invalidate it on navigation, logout, tab replacement, or extension heartbeat loss. Require explicit owner confirmation for an origin not previously bound.
missing: A browser_identity_attestation primitive that can be resolved against the extension’s exact tab identity and logged-in account without exposing credentials.
A signed, short-lived browser receipt consumed by /execute and joined to the action ledger.
A policy store for allowed origin/session bindings and a spoken refusal vocabulary.

args.user_asks: When you tell me something important, let me ask “why?” and receive the small set of source records that support it—what the pendant heard, what the relay stored, what the Mac/browser observed, and how fresh each source is.
args.why_useful: A fluent answer can otherwise hide whether it came from a stale memory, a browser observation, or an executed action. Evidence capsules make the system correctable and let the owner challenge one claim without exposing full transcripts, credentials, or private pages.
args.model_tier: Deterministic provenance index selects and redacts evidence; a background model can compress it into a readable explanation. Realtime is only needed to answer the spoken follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 s for a bounded capsule of up to five evidence items; if evidence is stale or absent, say so explicitly rather than filling the gap with model inference.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per explanation; indexing and redaction are local/relay compute, with model tokens only for optional compression.
args.security_concerns: Evidence is least-privilege and claim-scoped: no chain-of-thought, cookies, raw audio, or unrelated page content. Each item carries source, timestamp, integrity marker, and redaction status. Owner deletion of extracted facts must also remove their capsules, while action history remains intact.
missing: A claim/evidence ID attached to owner-facing spoken assertions and a bounded provenance query spanning pendant events, relay receipts, Mac jobs, and browser results.
A redaction layer that returns excerpts or hashes rather than whole transcripts/pages.
A retention and freshness policy for capsules, including explicit UNKNOWN when the source cannot be rechecked.

args.user_asks: My pendant or browser is not responding. Diagnose the whole path, explain the single most likely fault, and—only for safe repairs—fix it and give me a receipt; otherwise tell me exactly what I must do.
args.why_useful: Today failures look like silence, stale jobs, or repeated timeouts. A single owner-facing recovery path can distinguish pendant/link, relay, Mac bridge, and browser faults, perform only idempotent wake/restart/lease cleanup, and stop wasting the owner’s time on blind retries.
args.model_tier: Deterministic health probes and repair planner; a cheap background model ranks human-readable hypotheses. Realtime is only for the short spoken diagnosis.
args.latency_budget: Initial diagnosis under 3 s; safe repair under 10 s; revalidation under 5 s. Never claim repaired until a fresh post-repair probe passes.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per incident; probes and receipts dominate, with no model call for straightforward faults.
args.security_concerns: Repairs are allowlisted, idempotent, and scoped to the named surfaces: wake browser bridge, restart polling, clear stale command lease. Opening macOS permission settings is suggested but never represented as success. Preserve before/after health evidence and require confirmation for anything beyond safe repairs.
missing: A typed owner-facing diagnosis route that correlates pendant events, relay receipts, Mac jobs, browser leases, and system health.
A repair result schema with before/after probes, idempotency key, and explicit blocked-permission outcome.
A small spoken status vocabulary for healthy, degraded, repaired, and owner-action-required.

transcript.text:
Round 250 produced three new recorded proposals:

1. **Physical approval end to end** — stage risky actions, approve them with the pendant, execute once, and return a receipt.
2. **Claim-level provenance** — ask “why?” and receive bounded, redacted evidence for important answers.
3. **Cross-surface recovery** — diagnose pendant, relay, Mac, and browser failures; perform only safe repairs and verify them afterward.

Also recorded a relay change to add job leases, idempotent recovery, and correct action-ledger closure so crashes do not leave work stuck or duplicate unrepeatable actions.

Still needed:

- **Browser identity attestation**: exact logged-in account/tab/origin binding before browser actions.
- **Owner confirmation policy**: when spoken confirmation is mandatory versus when physical pendant approval is required. This request is already pending and should not be reissued.
- For the approval flow, implementation remains needed for relay persistence and next-conversation delivery of pending approvals; the pendant cannot currently be interrupted with an unsolicited approval prompt.
- For recovery, production wiring is still needed between the granted diagnosis/repair capability and the actual Mac/browser health routes.

args.user_asks: Give me a temporary, narrowly scoped delegation—such as “handle this one site and task for ten minutes”—that I can revoke from the pendant, and refuse every action outside that exact scope.
args.why_useful: Today the Mac, browser, relay, and approval routes effectively share one broad bearer authority. A single mistake or compromised session can reach beyond the owner’s spoken intent. Scoped delegation would let the owner safely hand over a bounded task without granting the system general control.
args.model_tier: Deterministic capability-token issuance, scope matching, expiry, revocation, and enforcement; realtime model only translates the owner’s request into a proposed scope and reads back the final boundary.
args.latency_budget: Scope preview under 1 s; pendant revocation effective within one heartbeat and under 2 s locally; every action checks the token before dispatch.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per delegation, mostly deterministic signing and audit writes; no model call is required for enforcement.
args.security_concerns: Use an audience-bound, short-lived, signed token containing allowed surfaces, origin/path patterns, action classes, resource IDs, maximum spend/volume, expiry, and a revocation epoch. Never pass cookies or secrets into the token. Default deny on ambiguous scope, navigation, account change, stale heartbeat, or relay uncertainty. Preserve an immutable issuance/revocation/action audit trail.
missing: A real authorization boundary distinct from the single AGENT_TOKEN, enforced by relay, Mac executor, and browser bridge.
A scope compiler that turns spoken intent into a reviewable allowlist and refuses unsupported constraints rather than broadening them.
Pendant delivery and revocation acknowledgements that work across link loss, with fail-closed expiry on every surface.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability:

**Scoped, revocable delegation**

The owner should be able to say, for example:

> “Handle this task only on this site for ten minutes.”

The system would issue a narrowly bound permission covering specific surfaces, origins, resources, action types, limits, and expiry. The owner could revoke it from the pendant, and every relay, Mac, and browser action would fail closed if it exceeded that scope, encountered an unexpected account/navigation change, or lost authorization freshness.

This is unavailable today because:

- `/execute`, browser actions, and approval routes share a broad bearer authority.
- There is no enforced authorization boundary between relay, Mac, and browser.
- No scope compiler turns spoken intent into a reviewable allowlist.
- No cross-surface revocation epoch or fail-closed token enforcement exists.
- Pendant delivery and revocation acknowledgements need to work across link loss.

The capability was successfully recorded via `propose_capability`.

args.user_asks: “Show me what you inferred about me, let me delete any one item, and prove the deletion reached every copy.”
args.why_useful: The system currently extracts facts into facts.json/context graph that the owner cannot see. This makes hidden memory safer: the owner can inspect recognizable evidence, delete one fact and its derived copies, and receive requested-and-pending status for relay replicas instead of a false instant-erasure claim.
args.model_tier: Deterministic retrieval and deletion planning; use the expensive realtime model only to turn a spoken reference into the correct fact candidate, never to decide deletion scope.
args.latency_budget: List under 2 s locally; deletion receipt under 3 s for Mac copies, with asynchronous relay convergence and an explicit pending state.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per invocation when voice disambiguation is needed; dominated by one small realtime turn, not storage.
args.security_concerns: Only facts extracted without an explicit owner request are eligible. Show source/evidence capsule before deletion. Require physical_transaction_approval_latch for deleting an ambiguous or multi-copy fact. Preserve action history, but erase the fact, derived copies, and evidence capsule as one scoped operation.
missing: A typed fact inventory route with stable fact IDs and evidence references
A deletion coordinator that fans out to facts.json, context graph, and relay replicas
A signed convergence receipt and dashboard/voice presentation
A policy distinguishing owner-requested memory from unsolicited extraction

args.user_asks: “When I pull the privacy latch, make the entire hive go dark—not just the pendant—and tell me exactly when capture, playback, queued work, and browser exposure are stopped.”
args.why_useful: A local mute is not enough if the relay still accepts audio, the Mac keeps a capture job, or a browser command remains queued. This gives the owner one physically initiated privacy boundary with a verifiable cross-surface receipt, including stale-command rejection and recovery only after an explicit unlatch.
args.model_tier: Deterministic state propagation and convergence checks; no model call is needed except optional owner-facing wording.
args.latency_budget: Pendant mute immediately; relay/Mac/browser quarantine target under 1 s, with a bounded 5 s convergence deadline and a loud failure receipt if any surface is unreachable.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; one signed state event and a few reads. Operational cost is bounded cancellation/expiry work.
args.security_concerns: Use a monotonic latch epoch and device-authenticated enter/exit events. Reject commands created before the current epoch; do not delete audit history. Never claim converged if a surface is offline. Unlatching must require the local confirmation pattern and must not replay quarantined audio or browser commands.
missing: Relay-side privacy epoch enforcement on ingest, playback, and queued jobs
Mac/browser supervisors that cancel or quarantine capture and pending commands
A single authenticated convergence receipt joining all surfaces
A recovery policy for work interrupted by the latch

args.user_asks: “After a crash or link drop, tell me which parts of the thing I asked for actually happened, resume only safe-to-repeat parts, and ask me before anything that could happen twice.”
args.why_useful: The code already records durable step state and can classify replay safety, but no production trigger closes ledgers or resumes them. Wiring this into a user-visible recovery report prevents duplicate messages, half-finished browser work, and the dangerous fiction that a queued job is either wholly done or wholly undone.
args.model_tier: Deterministic ledger/replay decisions; background model only summarizes a recovery plan in plain language.
args.latency_budget: Recovery diagnosis under 2 s after reconnect; safe idempotent steps may resume automatically, while unrepeatable/unknown steps wait for the next conversation and physical approval where required.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.005 per recovery; mostly local/relay reads, with optional cheap summarization.
args.security_concerns: Gate automatic replay on replaySafety (idempotent/additive), not reversibility. Bind resume to plan digest, world fingerprint, job lease, and expiry. Never auto-repeat unrepeatable/unknown actions. Preserve receipts and expose every skipped/blocked step.
missing: Production closeLedger calls for ordinary plans
A relay job lease_until and requeue sweep
A startup/reconnect trigger that invokes planResume
A user-facing recovery route and pendant delivery on the next conversation
A relay implementation of action handoff state

args.user_asks: “Before you act on a website, say which account, organization, and exact tab you will use; refuse if you cannot prove the identity, and show me the proof afterward.”
args.why_useful: A logged-in browser session can silently be the wrong account or tenant. Existing browser actions can click and type but do not give the owner a cryptographic, least-privilege identity/target attestation. This prevents sending, purchasing, editing, or publishing in the wrong place even when the page looks familiar.
args.model_tier: Deterministic browser/session attestation and policy checks; use the planner model only to interpret the requested target, never to infer identity from page appearance.
args.latency_budget: Preflight under 1 s for an already-attested tab; block and explain within 2 s when identity evidence is missing. Post-action receipt under 2 s.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.005 per action; dominated by browser snapshot/receipt storage, not model inference.
args.security_concerns: Never treat visible profile names or page text alone as proof. Bind an attestation to tab/session ID, origin, account identifier exposed by the site, and a short expiry; redact tokens and private page content. Require physical_transaction_approval_latch for irreversible or off-machine actions. If identity changes mid-plan, invalidate the plan rather than continuing.
missing: A browser_identity_attestation capability with origin/account/tenant evidence and expiry
Browser bridge hooks that bind attestations to command IDs and reject stale or changed tabs
A policy mapping requested target to allowed account/organization
A receipt joining preflight identity evidence to the resulting browser command

transcript.summary: Recorded three distinct capabilities this round: (1) a cross-surface privacy epoch that makes the physical latch quarantine relay/Mac/browser work and proves convergence, (2) crash/link-drop recovery driven by replaySafety with leases and explicit user-visible blocked steps, and (3) browser account/tenant identity attestation bound to command receipts so actions cannot hit the wrong logged-in account. The extracted-fact daily review was correctly rejected as an existing duplicate; I did not count it.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Two previously requested items remain unanswered: browser_identity_attestation and the owner's mandatory-confirmation policy for external actions. Implementation also still needs relay privacy-epoch enforcement, browser/Mac quarantine hooks, production ledger closure/resume triggering plus relay job leases, and a typed browser identity evidence contract. The owner must decide which accounts/organizations may be used for a given request; the system should not infer that policy.

The extracted-fact daily review was correctly rejected as an existing duplicate; I did not count it.
args.biggest_unknown: Two previously requested items remain unanswered: browser_identity_attestation and the owner's mandatory-confirmation policy for external actions. Implementation also still needs relay privacy-epoch enforcement, browser/Mac quarantine hooks, production ledger closure/resume triggering plus relay job leases, and a typed browser identity evidence contract. The owner must decide which accounts/organizations may be used for a given request; the system should not infer that policy.

args.user_asks: “Let me set a standing boundary such as ‘you may read my work calendar but never send mail as me, and never use the family account’; enforce it on every surface and show me when it blocked you.”
args.why_useful: Today authority is effectively one bearer token plus scattered action-risk checks. The owner cannot express durable, human-readable boundaries that apply consistently to the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. A policy firewall would make the system useful without requiring a fresh confirmation for every harmless read, while making prohibited authority impossible rather than merely discouraged.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy evaluation and command interception; a cheaper background model may translate an owner's spoken boundary into a proposed rule, but activation requires explicit confirmation and the final rule is machine-readable.
args.latency_budget: Evaluate each action before dispatch in under 20 ms locally; policy creation under 5 s including a spoken read-back. A blocked action should be explained on the next natural conversational turn.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per policy change and effectively zero per action; storage and evaluation are local lookups.
args.security_concerns: Default deny for ambiguous scopes. Policies must identify surface, origin/app, account/tenant, action class, data class, and expiry; no model-generated rule may activate silently. A stronger prohibition must override an approval latch, and policy changes themselves require physical confirmation. Keep blocked-attempt audit receipts without retaining page contents or message bodies.
missing: A durable, versioned authority-policy store replicated to relay and Mac
A single pre-dispatch policy hook for Mac actions, browser commands, relay jobs, and pendant-triggered requests
A typed policy language for account, origin, data, and action scopes with deny-overrides-allow semantics
A dashboard and pendant read-back showing the exact rule, version, and blocked reason
A safe spoken rule compiler with ambiguity detection and physical activation confirmation

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **owner-defined authority boundaries** enforced across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser.

The owner would be able to say things like:

- “Read my work calendar, but never send mail as me.”
- “Never use the family account.”
- “Only modify files inside this folder.”

To make it real, the system needs:

- A durable, versioned policy store replicated across surfaces.
- One pre-dispatch policy hook for every Mac action, browser command, relay job, and pendant-triggered request.
- Explicit account, origin, data, and action scopes with deny-overrides-allow behavior.
- Spoken rule read-back plus physical confirmation before activation.
- Receipts explaining which rule blocked or permitted each action, without retaining private page contents.

args.user_asks: When I say “make sure this gets done,” carry it through every surface and tell me only when there is proof it happened—or exactly what blocked it.
args.why_useful: Turns the pendant from a planner that can claim success into an accountable operator: it can execute on the Mac/browser, verify the result against bound evidence, recover safe failures, and leave an explicit pending state instead of silently losing the promise.
args.model_tier: background for plan/evidence synthesis; realtime only for the spoken acknowledgement
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge intent in under 2 s; safe execution and verification may take up to 60 s, with progress spoken only at meaningful state changes.
args.cost_estimate: Usually 1 background planning call plus 1 cheap evidence call; roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on browser complexity. Mac/browser execution dominates latency, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Evidence queries must stay bound to explicitly named tabs/apps and redact secrets. Irreversible or unrepeatable steps require the existing physical transaction approval latch. Never say done from an executor receipt alone.
missing: A production orchestrator caller for the existing commitment_evidence_query and workbench handoff primitives
A durable commitment state that joins spoken promise, plan digest, job, evidence candidates, and final disposition
Safe automatic retry only for replaySafety idempotent/additive; human continuation for unrepeatable/unknown
A user-facing pending/blocked view on the dashboard

args.user_asks: Show me what this system has inferred about me, one fact at a time, and let me say “forget that” so it disappears everywhere except the action audit trail.
args.why_useful: The system currently can extract private facts invisibly. This gives the owner an understandable privacy boundary: inspect the exact fact and evidence it came from, then erase the fact, derived copies, and evidence capsule as one auditable operation.
args.model_tier: background for grouping and plain-language rendering; deterministic code performs scope calculation and deletion
args.latency_budget: List first page in under 2 s; deletion receipt in under 5 s locally, with off-machine replicas explicitly marked requested-and-pending.
args.cost_estimate: One small background summarization call per page, typically under $0.01; storage enumeration and deletion are deterministic.
args.security_concerns: Never expose raw audio by default. Require a physical confirmation for erasure, preserve action/job audit history, show every derived copy targeted, and distinguish local completion from relay replication pending.

A cascade-erase transaction spanning facts.json, context graph, and relay replicas

args.change: Add a cross-surface ‘state of delivery’ record for every assistant response: correlate relay acceptance, pendant receipt, bridge playback start/finish, interruption reason, and any queued retry under one opaque artifact ID. Expose a compact owner-facing timeline and make missing downstream receipts expire into an explicit unknown state rather than success.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the pendant is silent, the owner can ask “did you answer me, or did the audio never arrive?” and get a truthful answer instead of a false successful job status.
args.effort: Medium: extend the existing audio_delivery_ack_queue contract, add relay correlation and a small dashboard timeline, then instrument bridge/pendant event emitters. Test with the existing 24 kHz validator and fault injector.
args.risk: Event loss or clock skew could produce unknown rather than false certainty; use monotonic sequence numbers, idempotent event IDs, bounded retention, and clearly label inferred versus device-confirmed states. Never store routine raw audio.

args.latency_impact: No hot-path audio delay if events are fire-and-forget; owner timeline may lag by one polling interval.
args.security_impact: Opaque IDs and redacted metadata only; no transcript/audio in the receipt. Access must follow the existing bearer/session binding.

audio_path_diagnostic_fixture (s16-dbfs) for repeatable end-to-end event tests

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: Watch this logged-in page for the condition I named, and when it appears, prepare the next step—but never submit or send anything until I physically approve it on the pendant.
args.why_useful: This is the first useful form of unattended browser work: the relay can wait while the Mac sleeps or the page changes, the browser can use the owner’s existing authenticated session, and the pendant remains the authority for an irreversible submit. It avoids polling manually and avoids giving the browser an unbounded autonomous agent.
args.model_tier: background for condition extraction and page-state comparison; deterministic browser polling and approval state machine; realtime only to explain status when asked
args.latency_budget: Create watch in under 3 s; poll at a configurable 15–120 s cadence; surface a match within one poll; approval-to-submit under 5 s.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost after setup; one background call to compile the condition and occasional cheap calls only when page structure changes. Browser polling and relay storage dominate.
args.security_concerns: Bind the watch to an exact tab/session and URL pattern, redact page contents from relay logs, cap lifetime and poll count, and invalidate on navigation/login change. The prepared action must carry a digest/world fingerprint and require the existing physical_transaction_approval_latch; never accept approval from page text or a stale spoken phrase.

A browser snapshot-diff matcher that returns bounded evidence rather than raw page dumps

args.user_asks: Stop everything you are currently doing for me, cancel queued browser and Mac work, revoke any pending approvals, and tell me what could not be stopped.
args.why_useful: A single emergency stop is more useful than hunting through jobs or tabs when the owner notices an unsafe or unwanted action. It would coordinate relay claims, Mac jobs, browser leases, staged transactions, and pendant playback, then report residual risk instead of pretending cancellation is instantaneous.
args.model_tier: deterministic control plane; no model required except optional plain-language summary
args.latency_budget: Local pendant mute/cancel immediately; relay cancellation receipt under 2 s; Mac/browser acknowledgements within 10 s, with late completions explicitly reported.
args.cost_estimate: No inference cost. Small bounded writes for cancellation intents and receipts.
args.security_concerns: The stop command must be authenticated to the owner session and idempotent. It may cancel reversible work but must not claim to undo an irreversible external side effect. Preserve the audit trail, revoke approval nonces, stop queued audio/playback, and distinguish cancel-requested, cancelled, and already-committed.
missing: A correlated cancellation fan-out endpoint spanning relay jobs, Mac jobs, browser commands, workbench contexts, and pending approvals
A durable cancellation barrier that late workers check before dispatch and before commit
A pendant-visible acknowledgement path that works offline and reconciles on reconnect
A residual-effects report linking each non-cancellable step to its receipt

transcript.text:
Round 252 produced four recorded proposals:

1. **Proof-backed commitments** — “make sure this gets done” executes across Mac/browser, verifies evidence, retries only safe actions, and reports blocked/unknown rather than claiming success.
2. **Delivery-state correlation** — correlate relay acceptance, pendant receipt, bridge playback, interruptions, and retries under one artifact ID.
3. **Condition-triggered browser watches** — monitor a bound logged-in tab, stage an action when a condition appears, and require physical pendant approval before submission.
4. **Cross-surface emergency stop** — cancel relay, Mac, browser, staged approvals, and playback, reporting what stopped versus what had already committed.

The extracted-fact inspection/deletion proposal was rejected as an existing duplicate, so I did not rephrase it.

Current discovery:

- **Safari:** online with two tabs.
- **Mac bridge:** online.
- **Cloudflare contract test device:** offline.
- The newly granted tools are available, including workspace editing, audio validation/fault injection, fleet diagnosis, evidence queries, privacy convergence, and incident diagnostics.

What is still needed to make the recorded proposals real:

- Relay-side implementation of browser-watch leases and approval delivery.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Owner-authored cross-surface policies**  
   The owner can say “never send messages without showing me the recipient” and have that rule enforced consistently across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. This requires a policy DSL, a shared pre-dispatch enforcement hook, policy versioning, and inspectable allow/block receipts.

2. **Local data-boundary enforcement**  
   Sensitive browser pages and files remain on the Mac unless explicitly approved for release, with a precise account of what left the machine. This requires local classification, field/region-level browser redaction, an egress gate, and an exposure ledger.

3. **Confirmed emergency escalation**  
   A configured pendant phrase or physical confirmation starts a durable emergency workflow, showing what will be shared and retrying until acknowledged or cancelled. This requires owner-configured contacts and policy, relay escalation state, offline pendant behavior, delivery receipts, optional location support, and iOS/browser adapters.

The main missing pieces are not individual routes; they are **cross-surface enforcement and durable state machines between existing routes**. The current system has execution, browser control, receipts, and health primitives, but no common policy gate, data-egress boundary, or emergency escalation coordinator.

missing: Complete the existing audio_delivery_ack_queue across relay, bridge, and pendant firmware
Correlate uplink capture, Opus packet ranges, bridge acknowledgements, playback start/finish/interruption, and link faults under one turn ID

args.user_asks: When I ask you to buy something in my logged-in browser, read back the exact item, seller, total, delivery address, and return policy; let me approve that exact checkout on the pendant; then submit once and bring me the browser’s confirmation receipt.
